In contrast, all of the responses that EAGLi provides are to inquiries of the definition types of questions.

articleTitle: MedDQN: A Deep Reinforcement learning approach for Biomedical Image classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The categorization of medical pictures is crucial for biomedical research and treatment, yet real-world data are sometimes difficult to use because of uneven class distributions. Conventional classification algorithms frequently fall short in such scenarios, rendering their effectiveness in doubt, particularly when faced with highly imbalanced data distributions. This study offers a novel approach to this pressing problem: a thorough unbalanced classification model based on deep reinforcement learning. Through the use of a deep Q-learning network, the method reframes the classification problem as a sequential decision-making process. Within this dynamic setting, an agent takes on the responsibility of classifying individual samples at each temporal step, while the environment assesses these actions and furnishes the agent with feedback in the form of rewards. Notably, the reward system is strategically calibrated to accord greater importance to minority class samples, thereby enhancing the agent's sensitivity toward these often-underrepresented instances. Our model systematically adjusts an ideal classification policy under the constraints of unbalanced data as a consequence. Achieving this goal is facilitated by the presence of a well-defined reward system and a nurturing learning environment. Its remarkable ability to not only identify but also accurately classify a larger number of minority class samples underscores its exceptional performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Kubernetes Auto-Scaling: Leveraging Metrics for Improved Workload Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Kubernetes is an open-source production-grade container orchestration platform, that can enable high availability and scalability for various types of workloads. Maximizing the performance and reducing the cost are two major challenges modern applications encounter. To achieve this, resource management and proactively deploying resources to meet specific application requirements becomes utmost important. Adopting Kubernetes auto-scaler to fit one’s needs are important to maximize the performance. This study aims to perform a comprehensive analysis of Kubernetes auto-scaling policies. This paper also lists out the various parameters considered for auto-scaling, and prediction methods used to efficiently handle resource requirements of applications. The research findings reveal a scarcity in the existing work regarding the variety of workload based auto-scaling and custom metrics. This paper provides a concise overview of a forthcoming research endeavor that explores the utilization of custom metrics in conjunction with auto-scaling.

articleTitle: Brown Rust Disease Detection Using CNN-Random Forest Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The research provides a thorough analysis of the CNN-Random Rainforest method for distinguishing wheat leaf diseases, categorizing them into Disease Intensity Level1 towards Disease Intensity Level5 groups. The model's extraordinary ability to properly identify wheat leaf illnesses and reduce incorrect predictions is highlighted by the fact that each class exhibits excellent precision, recall, and the F1-s all above 97%. The actual examples for each class can be found in the "support" column and range from 1030 to 1220, indicating a sizable dataset representation. The "support proportion" emphasizes a balanced dataset essential for an objective assessment. The model demonstrates accurate categorization with a 0.99 accuracy consistently observed across all classes. The "macro average" presents an overall performance picture with an F1-score, recall, and precision total of 97.39%. Given the makeup of the dataset, the "weighted average" retains this excellent performance at 97.40%. Reiterating this constancy, the "micro average" achieved an exceptional 97.40%. These reliable evaluation metrics confirm the practical applicability of the CNN-Random Forest technique in agricultural settings and demonstrate its effectiveness in detecting a range of wheat leaf diseases. The model excels in identifying wheat leaf diseases as seen by its excellent recall, precision, and F1-score, balanced representation, and noteworthy accuracy.

articleTitle: Accurate Anthracnose Disease Classification using a Hybrid CNN-Random Forest Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Using a strong classification model, this research work examines mango powdered leaf disease evaluation and mitigation. The research findings should summarised in the table below, which also shows how well the model performed in each of the ten categories of disease severity. Precision measures, which range from 94.70% to an astonishing 98.04%, highlight the model's accuracy in forecasting intensity levels. These metrics demonstrate its capacity to minimize false positives and match expected positives to real occurrences. Recall metrics, with recall percentages ranging from 95.43% to 98.28%, show the model's capacity to recognize true positive cases across intensity categories. The stronger recall is demonstrated at higher intensity levels, demonstrating the model's capacity to recognize complicated cases. The model's ability to strike a balance between precise predictions and thorough coverage is shown by the F1-Score, which combines precision and recall. The performance ranges from 95.06% and 98.16% and is steady. While support proportions provide a relative distribution, support values give precise occurrence counts. These revelations shed light on the class distribution and confirm metric importance over the entire dataset. Different stages of the mango powdered leaf disease have been accurately identified by the model. The thorough analysis, as shown in the table, provides information on how to fight sickness. This study contributes to data-driven disease detection methods and plant pathology.

articleTitle: Enhancing Generalization in Sparse Reward Environments: A Fusion of Reinforcement Learning and Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This paper investigates the viability of merging attributes of reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms to enhance agent learning in reward-sparse environments. The primary challenge lies in the inefficiency of reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms to adapt and excel in reward-sparse environments. This research addresses this challenge by proposing an adaptive learning framework that merges the strengths of both approaches. The proposed framework combines convolutional neural networks and DDQNs with genetic algorithms to evolve and optimize agents for a specific video game, likely Mario. The reinforcement learning component trains neural network-based agents to play the game, while the genetic algorithm component evolves a population of agents with varying strategies and characteristics to further enhance performance. The framework orchestrates the training process through generations, tracking fitness scores, utilizing replay memory, and employing various strategies like mutation and crossover to refine the population. Additionally, the project employs visualization techniques to analyze the learning process.The results indicate that integrating Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Genetic Algorithms (GAs) leads to rapid fitness improvement in evolving agents, followed by a stabilization phase, with population size and time affecting the exploration-exploitation balance, and late-stage variations potentially breaking local optima. The proposed framework offers insights into hybrid learning dynamics and could be generalized to other domains beyond gaming.

articleTitle: A System for Regulation of Anxiety-based Symptoms
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Mental health and anxiety remains a prevalent social issue and continues to affect millions of individuals globally. Despite this, there is a social stigma that revolves around seeking professional help for the regulation of mental health-related symptoms. Due to this, individuals opt for self-help techniques even though they do not serve as a long-term solution for this issue. A new approach to regulating mental health and anxiety-related symptoms is adopted. A wearable device equipped with bio-tracking sensors namely Heart Rate or Photoplethysmography (PPG) and Skin Conductance or Electrodermal Activity (EDA) accompanied by a smartphone application is developed in this study. The application provides the user with real-time feedback and analysis based on the bio-monitoring data collected by the wearable device and personalised guidance for anxiety regulation based on Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT). The device also consists of tactile feedback to gamify and reduce the effects of the anxiety symptoms. This systemic solution has the potential to mitigate the impacts of anxiety and its primary symptoms in the lives of millions of people worldwide, potentially improving their mental well-being. Future applications of Virtual Reality (VR) in anxiety regulation are also discussed in this study.

articleTitle: An Accurate Blood Pressure Prediction Based on Clinical and Physiological Data Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: When attempting to diagnose hypertension or cardiovascular illness, blood pressure (BP) is an essential biological feature. Taking a reading is interrupted and can be painful when done with cuff-based equipment like a sphygmomanometer. Recently, a cuff-free approach has been presented that uses electrocardiogram (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals. Due to the need for extensive multi-sensor collections, however, this approach is time-consuming and expensive. The current research uses a machine-learning(ML) strategy called classification-tree to examine the relationship between BMI, waist-circumference(WC), hip-circumference(HC), and waist-hip-ratio(WHR) in predicting hypertension(IBP). 400 college students, ranging in age from 16 to 63 (with women making up 56.3% of the sample), provided the data. In the training set, fifteen trees were generated for each sex by varying the number and order of predictors. Due to their low variance (89.56), low misclassification (.18), and high pseudo R2 (.43), BMI, WC, and WHR are the combination that yields the best anticipation for women. In the validation set, the model showed sensitivity of 82.54% and specificity of 83.68%, whereas in the test set, those numbers dropped to 45.65% and 65.15%, respectively. The lowest deviation (54.79), misclassification (.17), and highest pseudo R2 (.46) were found for BMI, WC, HC, and WHC when predicting male health. In the training set, this model showed sensitivity of 69% and specificity of 87.54%, whereas in the test set, these figures dropped to 58.38% and 69.70%, respectively. In the end, the classification-tree examination result was contrasted to the standard logistic-regression(LR) method, showing that the former was more accurate.

articleTitle: A Case Study on CALVEASE: AI Driven IoT Framework for Dystocia Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The ability to predict cow calving easiness cost-effectively, especially in the dairy industry where cattle suffer from a variety of unpredictable deadly illnesses and high breeding expenses assist farmers in improving reproductive performance and, thereby, farmers profitability. In this research work, machine learning and Internet-of-Things (IOT) based CALVEASE framework for monitoring dairy herd and predicting calving easiness is studied as a multi-classification problem. The CALVEASE framework collects activity information through sensors deployed in cow’s collar belt in the first stage. The collected information stored at the cloud platform is utilized to train machine learning models for predicting the cow calving easiness in the second stage. On empirically testing the various models during field testing, random forest outperforms the other models showing an accuracy of 99.58% hence, the tested framework was found to be efficacious for boosting the dairy herd productivity.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Diabetic Retinopathy Diagnosis:Harnessing Automated Deep Learning Classifiers for Early Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a prevalent microvascular complication of diabetes, often leading to vision impairment if not diagnosed and managed promptly. This paper presents an innovative approach for the early detection of DR utilizing automated deep learning classifiers. The proposed methodology integrates advanced image processing techniques with state-of-the-art deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs), aiming to achieve accurate and efficient DR detection. The initial stage of image enhancement involves the application of a Median filter to mitigate noise and enhance the quality of retinal fundus images. Subsequently, the segmentation process utilizes Fuzzy C Means (FCM) to partition the images into meaningful regions, aiding in the isolation of potential pathological lesions associated with DR. Texture features are then extracted using the Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) technique, capturing crucial textural information from the segmented regions. The extracted features undergo further processing through a deep CNN, which serves as a powerful classifier. The deep CNN is meticulously designed and trained to learn intricate patterns and representations in the feature space. By leveraging a substantial amount of labeled data, the classifier demonstrates a high degree of sensitivity and specificity in identifying early signs of DR. The amalgamation of preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and deep CNN-based classification culminates in an efficient and reliable tool for early DR detection and achieves accuracy of 98.67%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar Collector Temperature for Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: As the global population grows and governments everywhere restrict greenhouse gas emissions, household and business adoption of renewable energy sources intensify. Several types of solar collectors, including the Parabolic Trough Concentrator and the Linear Fresnel Collector, were employed to generate energy for the solar absorption system in this investigation. The thermal efficiency of the absorption cooling system was evaluated to see how its implementation would affect it. Solar energy was harvested using mature parabolic trough collectors and used into coal fired power stations of varying sizes regenerative feed water heaters. Since the recommended range for collector temperature increases varies with wind speed, researchers were able to determine the framework of the air temperatures allotted to activity and consistency as solar thermal power even while evaluating the local solar radiation strength.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Internet of Things Assisted Industrial Automation System with Smart Emergency Alert Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Environmental sustainability, energy and raw material availability, and globalization are just a few of the major societal concerns that are generating new demands on a wide range of societal players. Efficiency, adaptability, sustainability, and competitiveness are some of the new criteria. These have been around for a while, and a variety of systems have been tuned locally in terms of a few of these requirements, but recent developments with regard to communication and computational characteristics have made them much more useful to guarantee new possibilities for combining various parts of society, allowing for optimum performance on a scale that is far greater. The impact of IoT on several sectors of the economy has been substantial. The Internet of Things (IoT) is a technology that allows us to manage physical things over the internet in order to save time and energy. There are several factories in India because of the country’s rapid economic growth. However, industrial accidents were a severe problem in many sectors. However, industrial accidents were a big problem because they resulted in casualties and financial losses for businesses. This initiative aims to reduce the devastating effects of fires in high-risk industries including the oil, chemical and petrochemical sectors, where many lives and fortunes have been lost. It is crucial to have a system in place that can ensure the safety of the factory grounds and promptly alert the proper authorities should an emergency arise. In the past, a single bottle at a time would be loaded onto a conveyor and filled. This strategy is time-consuming and costly. Internet of Things (IoT) in Industries has been implemented to monitor and notify the individual in charge to take suitable measures in order to reduce manual overhead and therefore partially meet our needs. The manufacturing sector might benefit from AI-based management and oversight. “Ecosystem having Manufacturing Relevant Implication” better describes the Internet of Things than “modern technology.”

articleTitle: A study of Cardiovascular disease Risk factors using ML techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Worldwide, machine learning (ML) is applied in the healthcare industry. Machine learning approaches enable the preservation of cardiac illnesses and locomotor disorders in the medical data collection. Researchers now have a clear understanding of how to apply their diagnosis and course of treatment for a particular patient thanks to the disclosure of such important information. Medical professionals can identify diseases thanks to research using a variety of machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze vast volumes of complex healthcare data. In this paper, we used a 303-row, 76-property online UCI dataset for this investigation. It is crucial to evaluate the effectiveness of various strategies in order to assess about 14 of these 76 attributes. The isolation forest method makes advantage of the key characteristics of the data set.

articleTitle: Assessment of Wireless Technologies in VANET for Time Responsive Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: An area of the intelligent transport system is distinguished by its capacity to work in tandem with a smart transportation system to calculate, store, and rapidly deliver lag time messages to automobiles. Traditional vehicle networks have a range of resource deployment and issues due to a lack of scalability, flexibility, and connectivity. Linked vehicles have played a crucial role in the development of smart transportation infrastructure for autos in recent years as the smart city age has made it necessary. The wireless sensor network created by connected vehicle technology (CVT) uses a number of different wireless technologies, including RF, Wi-Fi, LTE, LORA, and others. Vehicles that are connected to the internet allow for V2V and V2I communication. In order for connected cars to function, sharing resources is essential. LTE V2V and V2I connectivity, as well as DSRC, facilitate this process. The content that transmits between linked vehicles is known as real-time information or data. Delays in real-time data transfer diminish WSN performance. There are several approaches for reducing the transmission delay time between connected automobiles. Because of the high mobility and frequent topological changes, transmission is delayed. Car-following models are also described in this article, and they play an important part in Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (C-ITS). C-ITS promises to improve road safety, traffic efficiency, and environmental sustainability by allowing vehicles to interact with one another and with transportation infrastructure. Car-following models are useful for facilitating cooperative interactions and coordination among automobiles in C-ITS.

articleTitle: Toward Accurate and Flexible Arabic Speech Recognition: A Comprehensive Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Continuous speech recognition (ASR/CSR) system for any language is crucial for the interactions between people and computers or machines. ASR systems play a crucial role in numerous applications, including voice-activated personal assistants and speech-to-text transcription. This paper mainly aims to outline the breakthroughs in CSR of the Arabic language and provide a comprehensive framework for Arabic CSR. Some aspects of speech recognition, like acoustic models, language models, and corpora, were addressed in this study. A review of current Arabic speech recognition(SR) research was conducted with a priority on Arabic-language speech. We outline the research approach, which combines both end-to-end(E2E) and modular-based approaches to improve the flexibility and performance of SR systems. The study proposed a comparhensive framework to build accurate and flexiable CSR system. This framework leverages the ensemble technique to integrate two CSR models, representing both the E2E and modular-based approaches. The study discusses audio capture, audio pre-processing techniques, feature extraction methods, and the utilisation of acoustic and language models. The study utilises machine learning techniques, including deep neural networks(DNN), hidden Markov models(HMM), transfer learning, and the ensembling of more than two models to train and optimise the ASR systems.

articleTitle: White Blood Cell Classification using Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: White blood cells protects human body from the various diseases. This study aimed to address the critical issue of distinguishing between different subtypes of Leukocytes (WBS) using deep learning techniques. Recent progress in biomedical diagnostics has been made possible by convolutional neural network (CNN) models, which have showed promise in automating the classification of white blood cell images. This proposed work introduces a unique CNN model architecture that can categorize white blood cell pictures into Polynuclear and Mononuclear classification. 12,500 images of white blood cells made up a large dataset that was used. With a batch size of 128 and a default learning rate, the suggested CNN model gone through intense training that lasted 30 iterations. The outcomes of this experiment show how successful the proposed technique is. When correctly categorizing the various white blood cell classification, the CNN model performed exceptionally well, obtaining a fantastic accuracy rate of 95%. For the discipline of medical image analysis, these discoveries have significant implications. This research adds to the creation of automated and precise systems for classifying white blood cell subtypes by utilizing the power of deep learning, particularly the CNN architecture. This CNN model's successful deployment sets the way for more complex AI-driven solutions in medical imaging, transforming healthcare procedures and enhancing overall medical decision-making. This proposed strategy can help with better categorization planning by allowing for the early identification of white blood cell subgroups.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting and Load Prediction Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Electric load forecasting is essential to energy management because it enables effective planning and resource utilization. Future electricity consumption forecasts must be precise. In this research, the effectiveness of ARIMA and neural networks— two widely used load forecasting techniques was evaluated. In order to get better outcomes, a hybrid model is suggested that combines ARIMA with an ANN. Three Statistical parameters—Precision, Recall, and F-Measure— along with the anticipated load served as the basis for the assessment. The results showed that the suggested model performed better in terms of prediction accuracy and error reduction than both ARIMA alone and ARIMA + Naive Bayes. In particular, compared to ARIMA alone and ARIMA plus Naive Bayes, the suggested model significantly reduced predicting error by 95.92% and 96.75%, respectively. These results show that the suggested model is a good option for estimating electric demand and may significantly improve energy management and planning.

articleTitle: Impact of Dataset Size & Data Source on Aviation Safety Incident Prediction Models with Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of dataset size on machine learning model performance in aviation safety incident prediction. We compare two datasets: the Aviation Safety Network (ASN) dataset and the National Transport Safety Board (NTSB) dataset. These datasets cover the years 2000 to 2020. Employing neural network architectures (LSTM, GRU, CNN, and RNN) and with advanced natural language processing techniques (NLP), we process textual narratives. Our findings underscore the role of dataset size in shaping predictive model performance. Larger datasets consistently yield higher predictive accuracy. Notably, despite having the same number of instances, the NTSB dataset outperforms the ASN dataset. Additionally, CNN stands out with better performance across various evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we examine the performance of these models on datasets of different sizes, affirming that larger datasets lead to better model performance, further highlighting the significance of dataset size in aviation safety prediction. This research emphasizes dataset size as a determinant of predictive model efficacy in aviation safety and suggests improvements in the data collection process for the ASN dataset. These insights resonate within the industry, underlining the need for substantial data collection efforts and the potential benefits of advanced NLP techniques. This study contributes to enhancing safety protocols and guides the broader machine-learning community toward boundless possibilities at the intersection of data, technology, and innovation.

articleTitle: A Logical Network Performance Improvement Design based on 6G Communication Support over WSN Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The development of wireless information and communication technologies known as 5G includes the incorporation of a number of different intelligent applications. Emerging technologies, on the other hand, have criteria that are noticeably less stringent than what the 5G specs specify. The amount of energy used per bit and the pace at which data is sent are also important aspects. Because of improvements to its frequency range, transmission speed, spectrum efficiency, connection capacity, latency, coverage area, and anti-interference power, sixth-generation (5G) wireless technology will be able to fulfill the needs of a wide variety of network configurations. The goal of 6G is to provide global coverage by connecting marine and non-terrestrial systems including communication satellites and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks for communication. To achieve this goal, terrestrial and extraterrestrial networks will be merged. Second, research into the sub-6 GHz, mm Wave, high-frequency signals in THz with laser frequency ranges will be conducted separately and in concert with one another in an attempt to increase data transmission speeds and connection densities. Thirdly, 6G networks will allow for a new class of smart applications with the help of AI and big data techniques in order to handle the enormous datasets that will be produced by the widespread deployment of these networks, the variety of interaction scenarios that will be possible, the large number of antennas that will be considered the norm, the expansive bandwidths, and the novel service requirements. In order to provide the unique service needs, such applications will be able to handle the enormous datasets produced by the usage of widely distributed networks, a wide variety of contact situations, and a huge number of antennas. In conclusion, the growth of 6G networks calls for increased network security. This article presents a discussion of the issues that have arisen as a direct result of current research on 6G technology and applications as well as a synopsis of that study.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network Technologies in Precision Agriculture-A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the main economic activities in India. Around 60% of the people are employed in agriculture. India has the world’s second-largest agricultural land. Over the years, the agricultural sector has seen substantial development, moving from ancient farming methods to contemporary and high-technology methods. Precision Agriculture (PA) is the management strategy that uses new technologies to increase crop yields and profitability by continuously monitoring, measuring and responding to various requirements of the farmer with the use of wireless sensor networks (WSN). Various wireless communication technologies are implemented in WSN such as Bluetooth, Wi- Fi, Zigbee, LoRa, LTE, and Sigfox, which are used for data transfer through the process of computing. This paper reviews the above-mentioned technologies and their use cases in PA. It also discusses edge and cloud computing with the use of wireless technologies in WSN for PA. The review of various wireless technologies in WSN with various use cases for PA carried out justify the importance of WSN as a essential tool for PA.

articleTitle: Forecasting Stock Market Using Artificial Neural Networks: A Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of stock market indices is imperative for investors, financial experts, and professionals, enabling them to make well-informed decisions and proficiently oversee their investments. This research conducts a comparative analysis of three forecasting models: RW (Random Walk), ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average), and ANN (Artificial Neural Network), applied to India’s prominent stock market benchmark, the Nifty fifty index. The dataset comprises daily adjusted closing prices of the Nifty fifty index spanning from January 2018 to June 2022, totalling 1106 trading days. This study employs two widely recognised error metrics, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), to evaluate the forecasting accuracy of these models. The results consistently demonstrate the superior performance of the ANN model over RW and ARIMA models, offering valuable insights for various stakeholders. The findings of this study have significant implications for academia, traders, investors, fund managers, and regulators.

articleTitle: Automated Clinical Note Section Identification Using Transfer Learning and Contextual Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The lack of structured formatting in clinical notes, often generated during patient consultations, contradicts established clinical practice guidelines advocating for structured formats such as SOAP. Building upon previous clinical note section identification research, this study employs Transfer Learning models integrated with clinical contextual embeddings for the automated classification of clinical notes into distinct major SOAP sections. Validated on a specialized dataset focusing on the cardiology department, the study substantiates the feasibility of developing intelligent note-taking applications using Transfer Learning. The potential for integration into Hospital Information Systems is highlighted, promising to streamline clinical note composition and address the issue of physician burnout.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques For Design Of Intrusion Detection System For Big Data Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: As digital technology advances, gigabytes and terabytes of data are now generated every second. Businesses in a variety of industries are finding that using the internet to manage their resources and transactions is useful. Given the value of data and the need to safeguard its security and privacy, securing big data remains a major challenge for all solutions. Due to the exponential expansion of network data, intrusion detection is becoming increasingly important, and manual analysis would be either impossible or take the same amount of time as analyzing it. As a result, there is an urgent need for an automated system capable of extracting relevant information from enormous amounts of hitherto untapped data when it comes to network intrusion detection. Data mining can perform a variety of tasks, such as clustering, prediction, classification, and the extraction of association rules between data pieces. In this research, we explore the application of machine learning methodologies to the task of creating intrusion detection systems for large data networks. As an input for this methodology, the NSL KDD data set is used. In the first step of this process, useful features from the NSL KDD data set are extracted using the CFS-correlation technique to feature selection. There are 41 features included in the NSL KDD data collection. Following the use of the CFS method, the total number of features was cut down to 16. Following this, machine learning methods are used to the NSL KDD data set in order to features the malware data and make predictions based on the data using the 16 characteristics.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Blockchain-based Privacy Preservation Approach for Internet of Vehicle Things
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: While studies have shown that Cluster-based Medium Access Control (CB-MAC) protocols are useful for administering and regulating Vehicular Ad hoc Networks (VANETs), these protocols need to be supplemented with a more secure and private authentication approach. Therefore, we propose a solution, named BPP-IoVT, to safeguard user privacy while using IoVT devices in transit. The paper explains in depth the processes involved in setting up authentication hubs, registering vehicles, and producing keys. To facilitate rapid handoff between vehicle sub-clusters, the proposed architecture utilizes a global authentication center (GAC) to store all vehicle data and a local authentication center (LAC) to administer a block chain. We also suggest a new control packet format based on the IEEE 802.11 standards to solve the issues with the current MAC protocols. In addition, methods for forming clusters, selecting members and a cluster leader, and merging and departing clusters are built with both safety and non-safety message delivery in mind. Through extensive trials, we demonstrate that the suggested BPP-IoVT technique saves both time and space in comparison to the state-of-the-art approaches. Numerical evaluations further reveal that the proposed BPP-IoVT protocols have superior throughput, latency, and packet-dropping rates compared to both standard MAC and benchmark approaches.

articleTitle: AI-weigh Live Tracking of Fruits and Vegetables
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Weight prediction of vegetables by analyzing without using a weight machine instead of using 3D live capturing AI powered trained model by combining (Mask R-CNN) algorithm with Marching Cube Algorithm, voxelization and computer vision technique to find weight. Leveraging advanced computer vision techniques, including the Mask R-CNN algorithm, Marching Cube Algorithm, voxelization, and deep learning models, the study introduces a nonintrusive and efficient method for weight prediction based on 3D representations. The methodology begins with dataset creation, comprising images of vegetables alongside known weights. Mask R-CNN is used for exact object identification, segmentation and to delivering essential ROI information. To build detailed 3D representations of veggies, we use voxelization, which turns segmented 2D ROIs into 3D voxel grids. The Marching Cube Algorithm is then used to convert voxel data into polygonal meshes, allowing for the estimation of surface area, which is an important aspect in measuring vegetable weight. We train a specific weight estimation model using a large dataset that incorporates calculated surface area as a feature. When presented with new vegetable photos, the system performs object identification, voxelization, mesh construction, and surface area estimate. The estimated surface area is utilized to generate an accurate approximation of the vegetable's weight. Continuous validation and modification guarantee that the system is accurate and resilient, taking into consideration real-world elements like vegetable density, wetness, and shape fluctuations. This study proposes a novel, non-intrusive approach for reliably forecasting vegetable weights, with possible uses in agricultural, retail, and food processing.Novelty: This research describes a novel method for determining vegetable weight that does not rely on existing physical weight machines. Vegetables are typically weighed using such machines, which can be sluggish and inefficient, especially for firms dealing with big volumes. Our method is a faster and more exact alternative to using a physical weight machine to measure vegetable weight.

Author Keywords: Density Values and computer vision technique

articleTitle: Enhancing Mental Health Care: A Proposed Approach for Depression Detection using CNN and LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In the landscape of mental health research, the detection of depression from textual content has gained paramount importance, promising crucial early intervention for those struggling with their mental health. This paper introduces an innovative LSTM-CNN model, meticulously crafted to analyze social media posts, online discussions, and blogs, showcasing a remarkable 93.41% accuracy in depression detection. This model, proficient in capturing both sequential intricacies and localized patterns, surpasses existing classifiers, firmly establishing its efficacy. This research marks a significant advancement in mental health technology, illuminating the potential of sophisticated machine learning architectures in revolutionizing precise and dependable depression detection. In an era where mental health support is paramount, this study heralds a promising future where cutting-edge technologies redefine our approach, ensuring timely help for individuals battling depression.

articleTitle: Exploring Societal Health Insights: Decentralized Distributed Topic Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The world can manage its paths towards better health thanks to the information, community, and support that medical forums offer in the modern digital environment. Integrating subject modeling on a decentralized platform may be essential and innovative along the way. Topic modeling aids in better understanding user requirements, spotting patterns and trends in the medical sector and taking proactive measures. A centralized platform is typically used to host health forums, but this has a number of disadvantages, including a lack of security and privacy for sensitive personal health information, the potential for bias and censorship to serve the vested interests of the central authority, and it is significantly more expensive to implement and maintain than a decentralized platform. We therefore suggest a medical forum with topic modeling housed on a decentralized platform to enhance the existing state of medical forums so that we can better understand the current topics of interest in the medical sector and act proactively. Topic modeling analysis speeds up reaction time and aids in better understanding community needs. Additionally, we recommend using sentiment analysis to enhance user experience through greater engagement, communication, and early issue detection. By analyzing patient feedback and opinions, healthcare practitioners will be able to enhance their offerings and patient happiness. Utilizing a decentralized network, the forum's host also offers several benefits like privacy, security, affordability, and less bias and restriction. The submitted information is not utilized by a central authority with personal interests.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Classification Models for Predicting the Adult Income Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Machine Learning was introduced before the 1960s,but has gained popularity in the recent years due to the exponential growth of data. Machine Learning algorithms enable computers to learn without explicit programming, and Predictive Analytics is a branch of advanced analytics that aims to make predictions about unknown future events. By analyzing historical data, machine learning algorithms can make more precise and accurate predictions, which can aid decision-making processes for various organizations. Choosing the most suitable machine learning algorithm is crucial for accurately classifying and predicting data, and this depends heavily on the specific dataset being analyzed. The task involves predicting whether an individual earns more than $50,000 per year, and various classifiers were evaluated based on performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall. The results indicate which Machine learning classification model is most effective for predicting adult income.

articleTitle: Exploring the Hazards of Embracing Decentralization in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Blockchain technology's decentralized nature has garnered substantial attention for its potential to revolutionize various industries. However, this decentralized approach also introduces a range of risks that warrant meticulous examination. This paper conducts a comprehensive review of the potential hazards linked to a decentralized framework within blockchain technology, focusing on technical, economic, social, and environmental dimensions. By identifying and understanding these inherent risks, stakeholders can make informed decisions during the implementation and utilization of decentralized blockchain solutions, thereby ensuring the technology's responsible and sustainable deployment.

articleTitle: Classification of Potentially Hazardous Asteroids Using Artificial Neural Networks and Over Sampling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of imbalanced datasets is a common concern in machine learning, particularly when dealing with rare events or outcomes. The issue arises when there are insufficient samples representing minority classes, resulting in biased models and inaccurate predictions. In this research project, we tackle the classification of potentially hazardous asteroids (PHAs), a task exacerbated by the imbalanced nature of the dataset. Our study utilizes the PHA dataset generously provided by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), containing crucial information regarding the orbital and physical characteristics of PHAs. To counter the class imbalance and enhance classification accuracy, we propose a novel solution employing oversampling techniques. Specifically, we leverage Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its advanced counterpart, Borderline SMOTE, in conjunction with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model for classification. By applying these techniques, we effectively balance the dataset, ensuring more representative samples for the minority class. This equilibrium leads to substantial improvements in the accuracy of PHA identification and a notable reduction in the risk of false negatives. Notably, in our results, we evaluate the performance using key metrics such as the F1 score and precision. It is worth highlighting that Borderline SMOTE outperformed SMOTE significantly, demonstrating its superior efficacy in handling the imbalanced data.

articleTitle: A Hybrid ABNB Model for Detecting Malicious Attacks for IIoS
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Industry 4.0 is no longer just a futuristic idea but is gradually becoming a reality, along with its key components, IIoT and IIoS. Industrial 4.0 introduces IIoT and IIoS technologies to improve manufacturing and production processes. IIoS and IIoT collect sensitive and proprietary data for automation and analytics, which makes industrial automated systems an attractive target for malicious attacks. Therefore, adequate safeguards and robust security controls are required for IIoS. Numerous machine learning strategies have been intensively studied to develop efficient and intelligent security measures. However, most of the current ML-based strategies experience difficulties when used on real-life operational grounds.The difficulties include uncertainty in determining the most appropriate ML approach based on an industrial model. Moreover, these challenges are aggravated by poor performance on inconsistent datasets and excessive rates of false positives. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to investigate the performance of various Machine Learning algorithms, including supervised learning (Nave Bayes), ensemble learning (AdaBoost), neural networks (MLP), and hybrid algorithm (ABNB), in detecting malicious attacks on three different datasets.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Approaches for Stock Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The stock market displays significant fluctuations, which are affected by numerous factors, including financial indicators, political events, environmental conditions, and a variety of internal and external forces. It has been a challenging endeavor, captivating the interest of both researchers and investors alike, due to its intricate and ever-changing nature. The objective of Stock Market Prediction is to forecast the future value of a company’s financial stocks. In contemporary times, a widely used method involves the application of machine learning techniques. These methods utilize current stock market indices and historical data for training to predict future values. Machine learning employs diverse models to enable precise and simplified predictions. Our study has overviewed the following methodologies which are - Neural Network, LSTM, SSA & SVR, SVM, Graph Construction, etc. After performing the comparative study, we identified LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) as the most appropriate algorithm for stock value prediction, taking into account factors like open, close, low, high, and volume. The outcomes of this study contribute to the growing knowledge in the field of stock market prediction using machine learning algorithms. The LSTM-based method demonstrates significant potential in effectively predicting stock prices, empowering investors and financial analysts to make well-informed choices.

articleTitle: Forecasting Economic Trends: Analyzing FRED Data with Time Series Methods and RNNs
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Time series analysis remains a vital field in data science, applicable across various domains, including finance, economics, and more. In this research, we use the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) dataset as an example to explore the effectiveness of diverse time series analysis methods and advanced deep learning techniques for forecasting. It’s important to note that our model is capable of handling numerous such datasets, making it a versatile tool for time series analysis and forecasting. Our comprehensive methodology encompasses collecting data from sources like the FRED API, preprocessing the dataset, and systematically applying a wide array of methods. These methods include traditional time series analysis, ARIMA models, and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architectures. Our findings highlight the power of modern RNN architectures, such as the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, in capturing the intricacies within time series data, exemplified here by the GDP dataset. These deep learning techniques, when applied to various datasets, exhibit remarkable accuracy and the potential to provide valuable insights for data-driven decision-making. While traditional time series analysis methods may have limitations in modeling the complex and dynamic nature of temporal data, they still offer valuable insights. This research contributes to the broader discourse in time series analysis, emphasizing the significance of modern deep learning techniques when dealing with intricate time series data. It provides a robust framework for practitioners and researchers to navigate the complexities of time series data analysis and underscores the utility of integrating these techniques for enhanced forecasting capabilities. The insights gained from this study hold the promise of facilitating practitioners and researchers, enabling them to make informed decisions when it comes to forecasting and analysis.

Author Keywords: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)

articleTitle: Exploring Recent Innovations in Text Summarization: Constructing a Sequence-to-Sequence Model for Enhanced Summarization
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The practice of condensing a larger text into a summarized version while keeping the major ideas and important details is known as text summarizing. Either a human being can accomplish this manually or computer algorithms can do it automatically. Text summary techniques have been developed by researchers since the 1950s. However, more recent summarizing initiatives also produced summaries from collections of publications. Most summarizing involves summaries of a single document. This paper assesses contemporary ways to summarize text in following categories: extractive, abstractive, and hybrid text summarizing. It also discusses specific strategies within each category. Furthermore, it discusses about implementation of text summarizer developed using sequence-to-sequence model and Long short-term memory (LSTM) model.

articleTitle: A Web-based AR Solution for Restaurant Menus to Reduce Food Waste
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This paper aims to reduce food waste using a web-based augmented reality (AR) solution called "Portion Perfect" integrated into digital applications helping customers visualise and compare dishes in a restaurant before ordering them. According to the Food Waste Index Report 2021, substantial food waste, contributing to negative environmental, social, and economic impacts, accounts for 8-10% of global greenhouse gas emissions. A framework is proposed that integrates transparency, visualisation, and personalisation to create an enhanced restaurant experience for customers. The AR part is built on Unity with the incorporation of the Vuforia Engine Software Development Kit and a mockup version of a digital restaurant menu is created on Figma. Furthermore, a mockup chatbot is integrated in the application to aid customers with personalised dietary restriction information. To conclude, this paper offers an AR-based solution to the problem of food waste via over-ordering. Future work would consist of prototyping the chatbot and creating a separate application which uses mobile laser scanning (MLS) to scan the three-dimensional models of the dishes.

articleTitle: DeepVision Attendance: A Visual Recognition System for Automated Attendance Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: It might take a while for teachers or administrators to manually mark each student’s attendance in numerous regular classes. By creating a visual attendance record utilizing facial recognition technology, this paper hopes to solve this problem. A collection of photos including the faces of people present in a certain class will be used by the system. The model will provide distinctive identification marks or patterns for each pupil by analyzing these photographs. When the camera is started using the created model, the system will instantly detect people and note their attendance. To achieve precise and trustworthy recognition of each individual, the technique uses the hog (histogram of oriented gradients) and Convolutional Neural Network methods. The project makes use of the OpenCV library’s capabilities to accomplish this, which offers a number of face recognition-related tools and features. This technique makes taking attendance easier and more time-efficient for both the teaching staff and the students.

articleTitle: SAndro: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Detection Framework of Adware Attacks on Android Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The use of Android machines is seeing a notable surge, characterized by a rapid rate of growth, owing to several factors that substantiate its significance in our daily routines. Adware is a kind of malicious software that exhibits the behavior of presenting unsolicited advertisements on a mobile user's device with the intention of providing advantages to the perpetrator. Adware, often known as advertising-supported software, is a kind of software that presents advertisements on a user's computer. Typically, these advertisements manifest as pop-up windows or banner displays. Adware inundates consumers with superfluous advertisements, so compromising their overall user experience. Attacker can have easy access the victim devices through adware attack. Artificial intelligence has shown to be a very efficient approach in the detection and identification of adware campaigns, with a special focus on smart machines, smartphone. This malware mainly communicated through ads on the website. Artificial intelligence employs advanced algorithms to evaluate user actions and identify malicious software, often known as malware. Signature-based detection and heuristic analysis play a crucial role in aiding artificial intelligence systems in the prevention of recognized adware problems by identifying and analyzing patterns and behaviors. In this research paper ensemble learning methodology is proposed to identify the adware on android machines using training with CIC-AndMal-2020 dataset and the proposed model is evaluated on the basis of metrics accuracy, precision, recall and ROC curve with respect to maximum depth.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Facial Expression Recognition using EfficientNetB0
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel deep learning-based program for Facial Expression Recognition (FER) using the EfficientNetB0 architecture. The program is designed to automatically recognize and classify facial expressions in images, an essential component in fields like human-computer interaction and emotional analysis. We employ two distinct image data stores for training and testing, both sourced from the CK+48 dataset, while also augmenting the data for improved model generalization. An image input layer, a pruned EfficientNetB0 network, an entirely interconnected layer for categorization, a Softmax layer, and a layer for classification make up out model structure. The efficiency of the model is assessed using a different test dataset after it has been developed via random gradient descent with momentum. Notably, we assess model performance using important parameters like accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1 score. The importance of this program rests in its potential to improve human-machine communication by training computers to recognize and react to emotional cues in humans. Its application spans a wide range of domains, including healthcare, marketing, and entertainment, where understanding user emotions is of paramount importance. The results obtained from this FER model can empower applications like virtual assistants and affective computing systems to provide more personalized and context-aware responses. The developed application’s robust architecture, training methodology, and evaluation metrics make it a valuable contribution to the area of FER.

articleTitle: Congestion Control Approach in Software Defined Network Using Buffer Size Parameter
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The software-defined network (SDN) allows a network administrator to shape traffic from a centralized control for which there is not any necessity of monitoring individual switches in the network. A centralized controller was employed for directing the switches so that network services are provided according to requirement without any certain connection amid a server and devices. An effectual path is required for transmitting the data amid devices to server. This route is established with a dynamic connectivity factor method. The link failure in the network results in load imbalance in the network. This research work presents a buffer size parameter in the dynamic connectivity factor technique for recovering link, and balancing the network load. In case of link failure, this technique employs the gadget of higher buffer size for recovering link. The novel mechanism is adopted and its comparison is done with diverse techniques concerning throughput, packet loss and LB.

articleTitle: System for Predicting Heart Disease using Sophisticated Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Cardiovascular illness stands as a significant global health issue, and timely identification of this condition holds paramount importance to ensure effective intervention. In this paper, we introduce a fused model for anticipating heart ailments. This amalgamation incorporates four distinct algorithms: LightGBM, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron, and AdaBoost. Through an assessment on the Cleveland dataset, AdaBoost emerged as the most accurate with a precision of 0.985. Subsequently, XGBoost followed closely with an accuracy of 0.980, succeeded by LightGBM at 0.956, and Multilayer Perceptron at 0.936. To harness the collective power of these models, we employed a weighted bagging technique that accords weights to predictions based on their individual accuracy rates. The resultant composite model attained an accuracy of 0.96. This outcome is slightly lower than the model with the highest accuracy, as it involves a weighted mean calculation across model predictions. This study indicates the potential utility of the proposed methodology in cardiac disease prediction, leveraging the ensemble approach to potentially outperform standalone models.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Role of Emotions in Elections using Bi- Directional LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Political campaigns are essential for candidate-voter connections and raising electoral awareness. Emotions wield considerable influence in these campaigns, making it vital for candidates to comprehend their impact. This study examines candidate speeches, views, and voting results, utilizing LSTM networks for emotion detection. The research explores the relationship between thought, communication, and voting, aiming to enhance democratic participation. The analysis involves preprocessing text data, converting it into embeddings, and using LSTM networks to predict emotions. The results reveal distributions of emotions in candidate speeches, emphasizing the role of positive emotions in successful campaigns. The visualization of LSTM embeddings using t-SNE, highlighting distinct emotional clusters. This holistic approach provides valuable insights for political discourse analysis, emotion detection, and future campaigns. Emotional appeals significantly impact election outcomes, with candidates evoking positive emotions garnering more support. Emotions like love and enthusiasm correlate with electoral success, while candidates tapping into discontentment may appeal to voters seeking change.

articleTitle: An Effectual Method for Clustering of Bigdata on the Cloud using Fuzzy c-means Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Big data clustering on cloud platforms has become increasingly important due to the exponential growth of data and the need for scalable and efficient processing. This review examines a paper that focuses on the application of clustering algorithms in a cloud computing environment to analyze and cluster large-scale datasets. The paper explores the implementation and evaluation of various clustering algorithms in a cloud-computing environment. It introduces the problem of big data clustering and highlights the significance of leveraging cloud resources to handle massive volumes of data efficiently. The authors propose a novel approach that utilizes cloud infrastructure to perform distributed clustering and present experimental results using real- world datasets. The paper provides a comprehensive literature review on big data clustering and cloud computing. It discusses relevant prior research, highlighting the gaps and challenges addressed by the proposed approach. The research provides evidence for the scalability and effectiveness of the suggested method when working with sizable datasets. It showcases the advantages of cloud-computing in terms of resource utilization and processing time.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis on Banking Customer Segmentation using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The intent of customer segmentation is primarily to aid institutions to custom-make their marketing techniques and methods to suit the specific requirements of every consumer group. As this helps to solve the segregating of the groups of customers for banks efficiently and helps provide more custom-made services for customers of each group better, applying the customer segmentation for banking data can provide many insights that can be beneficial to banks as well as their customers. This increases the effectiveness of customer interaction and can maximize selling opportunities. It makes marketers more efficient in terms of time, money, and other resources.

articleTitle: Word Embeddings and Document Topics are Combined With Deep Learning in a System for Classifying Videos
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: By empowering continuous discussions among an extraordinary number of clients, interchanges made conceivable by contemporary Web-based open doors have modified the manner in which people trade data today. However, the risks associated with personal assaults that force many individuals to quit a conversation in which they were taking part can occasionally undermine the benefits afforded by such potent tools of communication. Such an issue is associated with supposedly poisonous comments, which incorporate offensive attacks, individual assaults, and all the more extensively, a forceful style of support by many individuals in a discussion that makes a few members leave it. This exploration gives a methodology that might play out a multi-class multi-name order of a discussion inside a range of six classes of poisonousness by using the Apache Hadoop huge information stage and different word embeddings. Scientists test this technique by ordering a dataset of Wikipedia talk page remarks because of a Kaggle task.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Liver Tumor Segmentation: A Comparative Study of U-Net Variants for Medical Imaging Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Liver tumor segmentation(LiTS) is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, playing a key role in the early detection, diagnosis, and treatment planning of liver diseases. Accurate segmentation of liver tumors from medical images is vital for quantifying tumor size, monitoring disease progression, and assessing treatment outcomes. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and subjective, highlighting the need for automated and reliable deep learning-based methods. This study aims to evaluate and compare the performance of deep learning architectures: U-Net and its variants (U-Net, U-Net++, and newly introduced U-Net Square, and U-Net Cube) for segmenting liver tumors using medical imaging data. Each variant’s unique architectural modifications are examined, emphasizing their potential benefits for liver tumor segmentation tasks. The efficacy and performance of these models for detecting liver tumors is analyzed using metrics like Dice Coefficient. It is observed that basic U-Net outperforms other architectures in liver tumor segmentation. This study further provides potential implications for enhanced diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning in clinical practice. The results contribute valuable insights into the strengths and limitations of U-Net variants, assisting researchers in selecting optimal deep-learning models for liver tumor segmentation.

articleTitle: Sentiment-Driven Music Recommendations: A Comparative Study of ML Algorithms and Chatbot Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Music serves as an individual’s steadfast companion, akin to a friend who stands by our side through various emotional states, In like manner, a diverse range of music should be accessible to resonate with the full spectrum of human emotions. Typically, music apps curate playlists based on the popularity of songs, which may not always align with our emotional state. Therefore, our objective is to enhance the user’s music discovery process by providing tailored music recommendations based on user’s current emotion. In pursuit of this objective, our study provides a comparative analysis of various machine learning algorithms, like Decision Trees(DT), Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Random Forest Classifier(RFC), Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN).We also created a sentiment analysis based chatbot that will interact with the user to detect its current emotion. We used a comprehensive dataset comprising 278k emotion-labeled Spotify songs taken from Kaggle, that was rigorously trained using above mentioned models and their performances were compared in accurately detecting user emotions. Our research contributes to finding the most adept model for inferring user emotions, and also provides an interactive chatbot interface, ultimately culminating in a more personalised and emotionally resonant music recommendation system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning-Based Early Prediction of Sepsis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Without prompt diagnosis and treatment, sepsis is a potentially fatal condition that can cause organ failure and death. In order to improve patient outcomes, sepsis must be detected early. The ability to predict sepsis before it develops to severe stages has recently shown significant promise thanks to machine learning (ML) methods. In this study, we compare and assess the effectiveness of different machine learning (ML) models for forewarning sepsis using a publicly accessible dataset. Patients admitted to critical care units (ICUs) are included in the dataset's clinical information and diagnosed with sepsis. In order to train different ML models, such as logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support vector machines (SVM), and artificial neural networks (ANNs), we will first preprocess the data, extract pertinent features, and then train a variety of ML models. We will assess these models' accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC) performance. Our results will provide insights into the most effective ML algorithm for a quick diagnosis of sepsis. This research can help clinicians make informed decisions and improve patient outcomes by predicting sepsis before it progresses to severe stages.

articleTitle: Exploring Enhanced Localization Techniques: LIDAR-SLAM for Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This project outlines the development of a mobile localization robot using ROS Noetic that is based on Lidar-SLAM technology. Using a RPlidar sensor and the SLAM algorithm, the robot is designed to locate its position and direction in an unknown environment, scanning its surroundings and localizing itself. The system is built with ROS, a popular robotics framework, and operates on the Ubuntu 20.0 virtual OS running on a MacOS Monterey host system, which provides an energy-efficient robotics hardware. The method employed in this study, Lidar-SLAM, creates a 2D representation of the environment and evaluates the robot's location and direction by analysing the point cloud data captured by the Lidar sensor. The robot has a differential drive system, which allows it to move and turn precisely in small places. The Arduino uno microcontroller present on the differential drive communicates with ROS via a USB serial peripheral between the Arduino and macOS host system. The proposed system has the potential to undergo real-world testing by placing the robot in an unfamiliar location and evaluating its performance based on how accurately it can localize and map the surroundings. This project provides a low-cost and small solution for mobile robot localization based on Lidar-SLAM technology, which can be scaled and utilized for a variety of applications including warehouse management, surveillance, and inspection. The ROS-based design enables for simple integration with other robotic systems and provides a comprehensive set of robotics development tools. With its low-cost and energy-efficient features, it offers an ideal base for further enhancing the robotic applications, particularly in remote or resource-constrained areas.

articleTitle: Object Tracing with Colour range filtering in HSV Colour space and Object Following with Ros2
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This study proposes a unique method for object tracing with OpenCV (Open Source Computer Vision Library) using colour range filtering in the HSV (Hue Saturation Value) colour space and object following with ROS2. The suggested approach combines ROS2 (Robot Operating System 2) with OpenCV on a Raspberry Pi as the primary processing platform, allowing for effective communication and coordination between the two frameworks. Objects are identified based on colour range filtering, by utilizing the robust image processing capabilities of OpenCV using HSV colour space. The data of the detected object is then smoothly sent to ROS2 for additional processing and tracing. As the central node, it receives input from a camera, uses OpenCV to perform real-time object tracing and transmits the outcome to ROS2 nodes. Through this integration, OpenCV and ROS2 can work effectively together to give reliable solutions for object tracing and following. The feasibility and efficiency of the suggested strategy are demonstrated by the experimental evaluations carried out in a Raspberry Pi platform. The presented approach opens significant potential for many applications, including robotics, surveillance and interactive systems, where real-time object following are essential.

articleTitle: A Novel Elliptic Curve-Based Color Image Cryptosystem Using Transcendental Number
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In the modern world, securing digital material while it is being sent and stored via unsecured communication channels and databases is a highly challenging issue. Image cryptosystems differ from text-based cryptosystems due to the inherent qualities of images, such as their significant redundancy and capacity for large amounts of data, which are typically challenging to manage by traditional techniques. This article presents a novel color image cryptographic scheme based on a nice matrix created by transcendental numbers and elliptic curve cryptography. The proposed method successfully addresses the most essential features of image encryption: diffusion and confusion. The nice matrix generated by elliptic curve cryptography and the decimal expansion of transcendental number is used for the diffusion process. It employs the XOR technique to confuse the image pixels between the plain and cipher images. Also, Various experimental investigations are carried out and evaluated in detail, conducted with extensive evaluation, exhibiting the high level of security of the proposed encryption scheme.

articleTitle: Relative Analysis of VANET Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In city environments, routing remains a more challenging process for Vehicular Adhoc Networks(VANETs). In recent years, identifying an optimal end-to-end path that reduces overhead and delays has been challenging and limited. It is due to the increased movement of vehicles, the repeated failures of a path and the variety of obstacles that may impact the consistency of data routing and transmission that these limitations exist. Thus, this paper presents an enhanced VANET routing model that incorporates congestion, travel, collision and QoS awareness costs. Accordingly, in the proposed work, a cost model is modeled as the solution for the vehicle routing problem by taking into account the above-mentioned constraints. In addition, the Fuzzification of the QoS factor is considered along with the total routing cost. The work gets proceeded by intending to find the optimal route that concerns the minimized routing cost. For determining the optimal route, this research work establishes a new hybrid algorithm known as Grey Updated Butterfly Operator (GU-BO) that links both the concepts of Monarch Butterfly Optimization (MBO) Algorithm and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). Finally, the performance of the implemented approach is compared over other conventional approaches namely, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Firefly algorithm (FF), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WAO), Jaya Algorithm (JA), MBO, and Mean Computing Jaya Algorithm (MC-JA) with respect to convergence analysis and cost analysis, and proves its superiority of proposed work over others.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Agriculture through Leaf Disease Prediction in Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: India's agricultural strength is hindered by plant diseases due to limited understanding of disease markers and remedies. Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), offers hope for enhanced disease detection in agriculture. Our proposal centers on CNNs for accurate plant disease identification, streamlining the process. Urgency arises from economic repercussions and global food security. Deep learning is employed in various sectors such as healthcare, finance, and agriculture. Its applications range from identifying diseases, classifying weeds and leaves, to predicting soil moisture levels. The survey tackles current trends and objections in deep learning for plant disease prediction, guiding aspiring researchers. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) tools replace costly visual inspection. Our study deploys ML algorithms including K Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Random Forest(RF) algorithm, Naïve Bayes, Decision Trees, and Support Vector Machines(SVM) on a diverse crop image dataset. A CNN-based system, coupled with ML soil analysis, suggests fitting crops, enabling informed planting choices. Classifier comparison validates Support Vector Classifier's (SVC) superiority. Swift disease detection is critical for food demand and economic growth. This study proposes a modern evaluation system using ML and pre-trained models (VGG16, InceptionV3, ResNet152) on datasets to classify plant diseases. IoT further augments disease and yield prediction, vital for modern agriculture.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms for Benign-Malignant Breast Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Breast cancer is still a major worldwide health concern, and mortality rates are greatly impacted by late-stage diagnoses. Globally, late-stage breast cancer claims the lives of about 685,000 women each year.This study explores new developments in breast cancer detection, highlighting the importance of an early diagnosis. This article examines cutting-edge medical imaging methods and applications of artificial intelligence that could lessen this burden by increasing precision and enabling earlier diagnoses, ultimately improving patient outcomes and lowering breast cancer-related mortality. Additionally, we used three different classifiers—Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest—to thoroughly assess our expanded dataset.
