Because of their adaptability and appropriateness for handling complicated information, these classifiers were chosen. Our findings indicate promising results, with specific classifiers demonstrating increased sensitivity and specificity in early breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: Polynomial Fit-Based Linearization of NTC Thermistor and Construction of Temperature Alarm for HTST Pasteurization
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This study presents a novel method to transform the nonlinear resistance-temperature characteristics exhibited by the 334NTC103RC thermistor into a linear response suitable for industrial applications. This is achieved by employing a voltage divider circuit to convert the thermistor’s resistance value into an electrical signal. Subsequently, the least squares method is implemented within a microcontroller to linearize the initially nonlinear voltage output. The setup is then integrated into a real-time temperature monitoring system to ensure that the milk temperature is maintained below 72 degrees Celsius during the High-Temperature Short-Time (HTST) pasteurization process. An alarm system has been incorporated into the setup, which serves as a fail-safe mechanism, promptly alerting operators when the temperature exceeds the specified target, thus guaranteeing the consistent and safe production of pasteurized milk within stringent quality parameters.

articleTitle: Extracting Cryptographically Secure Uniform Random Bits from a Biased Sequence
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Random Number Generators (RNG) are indispensable in cryptography, network security, and statistical simulations. Most commonly available pseudo-RNG (PRNG) are known to produce non-uniform sequences. Natural and hardware sources of randomness are also prone to bias. Therefore, extracting uniform random bits from non-uniform sources of entropy is frequently necessary. In this paper, we look at the philosophical idea of randomness, the impossibility of determining unbiasedness with certainty, and the bias of natural systems. We then propose different methods of doing this, and evaluate them using the NIST statistical test collection. We find that hashing adequate number of bits from a biased sequence is a statistically robust, effective, fast, and efficient way to generate a uniform sequence.

articleTitle: Security and Privacy Challenges in Distributed Database Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the challenge of recognizing and evaluating distributed database management system (DDBMS) security and privacy challenges and also to describe important danger indicators that may lead to possible data security difficulties in distributing resources, both tangible and functioning. An investigation of the primary DDBMS security and privacy challenges that can be found while developing and managing a standard DDBMS meant for supporting data procedures and offering data services was conducted as a component of this research. The data assessment was produced depending on the findings of surveys and questionnaires administered to DDBS security and privacy professionals with varying degrees of training and emphases in their operations within this expertise field. The findings of the research include a list of primary risk variables based on their significance and frequency in practice, and also a spotlight on the most important security and privacy measures. This article summarizes data on traditional methods to illustrate data security challenges employing statistical, qualitative, and mixed evaluation, and also the most recent techniques depending on smart categorization and examination of DDBS security and privacy challenge factors and functioning with huge amounts of data.

articleTitle: Detection and Segmentation of Skull Fractures via CNN and U-Net Hybrid Model using Computed Tomography Images
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Computer tomography (CT) are now widely used for the diagnosis of head various head injuries. A CT scan slice has a lot of data that can’t always be thoroughly analyzed quickly and precisely enough with standard visual inspection. To help doctors, a computer-assisted skull fracture detection and classification expert system is required. The most widely used deep learning models for image classification are convolutional neural networks (CNNs), as their accuracy and output consistently beat those of other models. This research aims to develop a model with a hybrud model of CNN with a custom classifier, DenseNet-161 and U-Net, that shows an increased efficiency and ease, through detection and segmentation of the CT scan images in the CQ500 dataset. The model achieved an accuracy of 98.37%, AUC score of 0.972, Recall score of 0.88 and Precision score of 0.87. These results represent a notable improvement over other models.

articleTitle: Attention Unveiled: Revolutionizing Image Captioning through Visual Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Image captioning models are a type of "Natural Language Processing" (NLP) models that are designed to generate textual descriptions of images. These models are trained on large datasets of images and captions, and use a combination of deep learning models and natural language processing techniques to generate accurate and informative captions. These models have proven to be effective in improving the quality of the generated captions. In recent years, researchers have also been exploring the use of reinforcement learning, adversarial training, and other techniques to improve the performance of image captioning models. Specifically, techniques like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), where human-provided captions guide model training, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which generate captions through a competition between a generator and discriminator network, and Self-Critical Sequence Training (SCST), which optimizes model performance based on its own generated captions, have gained attention. These approaches aim to enhance the quality and relevance of captions generated by image captioning models. Visual attention models use a transformer and attention models typically consist of two main components: an image encoder that extracts features from the image and a language decoder that generates the textual description. This paper focuses on techniques that can be used for Image Captioning using visual attention models.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Efficiency for First Generation Solar Cells Using PSIM Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Solar photovoltaics from the first generation are well-developed in terms of their technology and how they are made. They are the oldest photovoltaics technologies that can be bought and sold. Most of the time, they are made from wafers of crystalline silicon (c-Si) or GaAs. GaAs is a direct bandgap semiconductor with a bandgap of 1.43 eV at 300 K. Compared to silicon, it has better optical properties. Silicon, on the other hand, has a bandgap of about 1.12 eV at 300 K and is an indirect bandgap material. So, silicon solar cells need silicon wafers that are thicker than other types in order to absorb enough sunlight. In this paper, simulation in PSIM was used to compare the efficiency of all first-generation solar cells in four different places with different amounts of light and temperatures. Any photovoltaic technology will work less well as the temperature rises. But even at higher temperatures, GaAs solar cells still work well because their temperature coefficient is so low.

articleTitle: Rice Crop Disease Detection Using Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The development of automated systems that use Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning Techniques has enabled the identification and detection of diseases in images with increasing accuracy and efficiency. In today’s scenario, farmers are facing many problems. They face challenges like poor infrastructure, lack of knowledge of emerging technologies, poor soil quality, investment in farm production, etc., when growing rice crops. In South India, many farmers need to know how to select fertilizers and pesticides for their rice crops properly. Due to the diseases that affect the rice crop, farmers and consumers face a significant loss. Nearly 60% of the farmers face losses in crop yield. As a result, there have been multiple reports of the deaths of the farmers. We identified the rice crop diseases and focused on specific aspects, including image dataset, no. of diseases (classes), and model accuracy. We created a model using Convolution Neural Network (CNN) for classifying images and explainable Artificial Intelligence (xAI) by using a local interpretability technique called LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) to explain the predictions that the model makes. This model can extract the features of the disease in the given image. Evaluation of the images from the Rice Disease Image dataset shows that our model’s accuracy is 91.60%.

articleTitle: An Integrated Framework for Vertical Farming in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This paper examines indoor vertical farming in urban settings, investigating its impact on food accessibility, food security, environment, and the resident’s well-being. Addressing food security is particularly crucial for low-income households in the global south, necessitating sustainable and locally sourced food to support their socio-economic progress. Challenges such as limited urban land, high transportation costs, and lengthy supply chains hinder traditional agricultural practices. To tackle these issues, an integrated framework for vertical farming is proposed, emphasizing practicality, modularity, and scalability. This framework consists of three sub-systems: a controlled environment for optimised plant growth, a smartphone application, GoGreen, for user education and community engagement, and policy guidelines encompassing zoning regulations, building codes, environmental standards, energy efficiency requirements, water conservation guidelines, and food safety regulations. Through rigorous testing and user feedback, the app’s accuracy was found to be 92% for controlled environment monitoring, ensuring optimal plant growth. By promoting sustainable urban agriculture and efficient resource utilisation, this framework generates employment opportunities and ensures food security for marginalised communities, particularly women and children, in densely populated developing areas.

articleTitle: Bilingual Chatbot Powered by Artificial Intelligence for Academic Advice
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The role of academic advising in advancing institutions' educational goals is becoming more widely recognised. Utilizing technology tools like Canvas and Degree Works, universities have made considerable investments in assisting instructional advisers and student success measures. The demand for innovation that can support academic advisors in their duty to direct students toward academic achievement is growing, and AI tools that encourage the effective use of human capital are well-placed to fill that requirement. Functions for chatbots can be used as technology-mediated assistance to give knowledge and engaging content to help students succeed. This project set out to create, build, and assess an automated, AI-enabled advising resource (the AVA chatbot) for use in an honour’s college setting to provide academic counselling and university-related information. The researchers came to the conclusion that chatbots could assist educational universities in efficiently supporting their student populations by giving 24/7 advice, following and evaluating total assistance, and identifying data perceptions in real time. The consequences of this research can be helpful for chat application design and manufacturing as well as technology adoption in higher education.

articleTitle: Mapping Research Clusters of Artificial Intelligence for Financial Services Using Topic Modelling: A Machine Learning Insight
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) improves decision-making and streamlines processes in the financial services industry. This study aims to explore the adoption of artificial intelligence in financial services over the last two decades. This research conducts a comprehensive analysis using bibliometric techniques and structural topic modelling on a dataset of 378 articles collected from the Scopus database, covering the span of two decades from 2002 to 2022. The primary focus of this study revolves around the domain of AI in financial services. It seeks to scrutinise publication trends, identify prominent sources, and uncover thematic clusters within this field. Remarkably, "The AI Book: The Artificial Intelligence Handbook for Investors, Entrepreneurs, and Fintech Visionaries" emerges as the leading source, contributing 5% of the total articles. The results obtained through structural topic modelling reveal the presence of five distinct thematic clusters, including topics such as financial services and customer management, AI and regulations, technology adoption in financial services, AI-driven risk management, and fraud detection in financial services. Future research trends in this field are anticipated to emphasise transparency, regulatory compliance, personalised customer experiences, proactive fraud prevention, ethical considerations, and the integration of quantum computing with AI for addressing complex challenges, ultimately reshaping the financial services industry landscape. These findings hold significant implications for many stakeholders, encompassing academics, practitioners, regulators, and policymakers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Plagiarism Detection Through Perceptual Hashing and Edge Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In a time when digital photography is so common, the significance of preserving the integrity of visual content cannot be stressed. In this study, a novel combination of perceptual hashing and edge analysis methodologies is used to improve picture plagiarism detection. This method's careful design is centered on the challenging problem of finding visually identical or altered photographs within the large digital environment. A useful method for identifying photocopying is perceptual hashing, which has roots in computer vision. It recovers unique image fingerprints that exhibit resilience to slight alterations. Parallel to this, we evaluate the intricate structural elements of photographs using edge detection techniques, making it simpler to discern copied content from the original source.

articleTitle: Dementia Diagnosis through Artificial Intelligence in Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Dementia, a progressive cognitive impairment affecting memory and cognitive functions, poses significant challenges for timely diagnosis and intervention. This work presents a comprehensive methodology for predicting dementia by harnessing the power of image processing and machine learning techniques. The preprocessing stage employs Gaussian filtering to enhance image quality by reducing noise and preserving important structural information. This step prepares the input images for subsequent analyses with improved clarity and noise resilience. Subsequently, Otsu's segmentation technique is applied to the preprocessed images. Otsu's method optimally segments images into distinct regions based on variations in pixel intensity, aiding in the extraction of relevant regions of interest that contribute to dementia prediction. To capture intricate textural details indicative of dementia-related changes, gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) based feature extraction is employed. GLCM quantifies the spatial relationships between pixel values, providing valuable insights into image texture. This feature extraction process yields a high-dimensional feature space that encapsulates complex texture patterns within the segmented regions. The core of the proposed methodology lies in the Probabilistic Neural Network (PNN) based classification. PNNs are well-suited for pattern recognition tasks due to their ability to model complex relationships in data and provide probabilistic classification which achieves accuracy of 97.82%. By synergizing these techniques, the proposed methodology showcases promising results in accurately identifying dementia improving the quality of life for individuals affected by dementia.

articleTitle: Grammar Error Correction using Monotonic Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Grammar error correction is an essential task in natural language processing (NLP), aimed at identifying and correcting errors in written texts. While various approaches have been proposed to address this problem, most of them rely on rule-based or statistical methods such as bayesian Networks, attention mechanism, monotonic attention and much more that have limitations in dealing with the complexity and ambiguity of natural language.Previously, the correction of errors mostly used attention mechanism, which assigns weights to the input sequence based on their relevance to the current output token. The assigned weights are then utilized to calculate a sum of the input tokens, taking into account the weight of each token, generating a context vector that informs the next step of the output generation process. This mechanism has been used successfully in many NLP tasks and grammar error correction.Here, we worked on monotonic attention in a model for grammar error correction, the model can improve its allignment accuracy, training efficiency, and overall performance. This can lead to more accurate and efficient error correction, which is essential for improving language proficiency and streamlining the writing process. The goal is to improve the performance of the model by reducing the amount of redundant computation and increasing the interpretability of the attention weights.

articleTitle: Human Action Recognition using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Identifying human activities from videos is a challenging area of computer vision that requires the recognition of human actions. In this work, we offer a Mediapipe and LSTM based deep learning-based technique for human action recognition. Using Mediapipe, we decode human stance and movement information from videos, and then we feed the information into an LSTM network to categorize the actions. We test our method using a custom dataset that we collected under a number of difficult conditions, such as shifting lighting, shifting camera angles, and occlusion. On our custom dataset, our suggested method performs at the cutting edge with a maximum accuracy of 96.3%. We run comprehensive tests to evaluate how well our method stands up to various scenarios, such as changing lighting conditions, shifting the camera’s angle and occlusion. Potential applications for our suggested methodology include surveillance, sports analysis and human-robot interaction among other areas.

articleTitle: AgroInnovate: A Framework for Sustainable and Smart Irrigation in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Agriculture is a fundamental global practice, reliant on optimal conditions for crop productivity. Agriculture, a globally embraced practice, demands optimal conditions for efficient crop production and yield improvement. This research introduces an intelligent irrigation monitoring and control system, employing Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The system leverages soil pH, moisture, and temperature data obtained from field sensors, storing it in the cloud. It allows manual and automated operation via a mobile app, with automated mode activating pumps based on soil conditions. Key parameters, including soil pH, moisture, and temperature, are sensed using on-field sensors, with data stored in the cloud. The system introduces dual operational modes, manual and automated, to cater to varying farmer requirements. In manual mode, farmers retain remote control, enabling the activation or deactivation of critical components such as the water motor pump, water sprinkler pump, and fertilizer pump, all via a user-friendly mobile application. In automated mode, pumps are triggered based on soil conditions, optimizing water and fertilizer use. The system also maintains ideal soil pH, promoting crop growth. Additionally, it manages soil pH by automatically adjusting fertilizer injection. The proposed system offers remote monitoring and control via a website or mobile app, aiming to maximize crop production while adhering to standard parameters. This research proposes a sensor module for parameter measurement and actuation. The system facilitates remote monitoring and control through a website or mobile app, aiming to maximize crop production while adhering to standard parameters. Upon detecting soil conditions falling outside the predefined threshold values, the system initiates automatic control actions. When soil moisture registers below the established threshold, the system automatically activates the water supply pump to ensure adequate irrigation. Conversely, when the soil temperature surpasses the defined threshold, the system triggers the water sprinkle pump to mitigate excessive heat and optimize crop growth conditions. This dynamic response mechanism, orchestrated by the automated mode, serves as an indispensable feature of the proposed system, enhancing its ability to provide timely and precise irrigation support based on real-time soil conditions.

Author Keywords: Sensing Devices Cloud Network: Cloud Computing

articleTitle: User-based Adaptive Search using Elliptic Curve Cryptography and Message Digest for a Secure Cloud Storage Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This work provides a user-based adaptive search strategy for secure cloud storage utilizing ECC and message digests. The method protects cloud user data and optimizes search processes. User-based access control and ECC provide unique encryption keys for each user, preventing cryptographic attacks. These keys encrypt cloud storage user data. Message digests condense encrypted data for efficient searches. These message digests are saved in a cloud index table for quick, accurate searches without sacrificing data privacy. The user encrypts their query with their encryption key and matches it against the index table’s message digests. A safe comparison protocol matches digests without disclosing the content, limiting illegal access. Adaptive search lets consumers change their inquiries without sacrificing privacy. Message digest data integrity checks identify unlawful data changes. Experimental results indicate safe and efficient user-based adaptive search in cloud storage systems. The method combines strong security, fast search, and data privacy by integrating ECC and message digest techniques. It is a viable alternative for those wanting safe cloud storage with increased search.

articleTitle: Segmentation of E-Commerce Data Using K-Means Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In this era of technology and development, every day large amount of data is being produced, collected and transferred. This data can be analysed by various machine learning algorithms and used as per requirement and interest of people. Companies can increase their productivity according to the interest of customers hence customer segmentation is being needed. It allows businesses to know and understand the needs and motivations of customer, so they provide a great experience and also launches the required and needful products. Businesses may better satisfy the demands of their consumers by customising their products, services, and marketing initiatives by knowing the distinct wants and preferences of various client groups. As a result, customers are more satisfied and loyal, which eventually boosts sales and income. This paper presents the analysis of E-commerce data and segment them on the basis of RFM variables. The customers are clustered on the basis of demographics and behavioural aspects, such as age, gender, marital status, etc. Elbow method was used for finding optimal number of clusters and total 3 clusters are formed on the basis of recency, frequency, and monetary. Now Business people can apply various marketing strategies for their interests.

articleTitle: Quality Evaluation and Assessment of Machine Translations for English to Turkish (Google Translations Vs DeepL Translations)
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This study aims to compare the quality of machine translation systems that handle six different types of text: intelligibility, fidelity, coherence, acceptability, usability, and reading time while translating from English to Turkish. To perform an evaluation, the system was evaluated using the criteria set by Van Slype in 1979. The end-users were also asked to assess the machine translation system's output using a questionnaire to determine if it was acceptable and understandable to them. The evaluation results revealed that DeepL translations are more useful than Google translations when translating certain text types. When translating some text types, the findings reveal that machine-generated translations are clear and acceptable to end users and that DeepL is more acceptable.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Optimization Based Support Vector Regression Algorithm for Performance Prediction of Wearable Textile Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Body-centric wireless communication has been made possible by textile patch antennas which have lately gained significance in wearable applications. They are used in a wide range of industries, including healthcare and defence. However, due to varying properties of substrate materials and complexity in the geometric features of patch antennas, it is often challenging to optimize and predict their performance in terms of gain, directivity and return loss. In this paper, an ant colony optimization-based support vector machine regression algorithm (ACO-SVM) is proposed for modelling the relationship between different antenna parameters and output performance (in terms of gain, directivity and return loss). An ablation study is performed to explore the role of operating frequency in determining the output signal strength of antennas. Experiments show that the ACO-SVM models this complex relation most accurately with the lowest loss values: Mean Squared Error (MSE) = 5.33, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.22, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) = 1.02, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Score = 0.13) and inference time of 2ms. To validate the model’s performance, a textile patch antenna is designed using HFSS with a range of fabric-based substrate materials (cotton, poly-amide, and polyester) and its performance is analysed in simulation. It is shown that the simulated results and the algorithmic results obtained with ACO-SVM agree well with one another and that the proposed ACO-SVM approach can predict optimal antenna design parameters given the required performance in terms of gain and return loss.

articleTitle: Food Recommendation System Using K-means Clustering and Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: A balanced diet is a cornerstone of a healthy lifestyle, with far-reaching effects on overall well-being and the prevention of chronic diseases. In our increasingly health-conscious world, the importance of tailored dietary choices has never been more apparent. However, achieving and maintaining a balanced diet can be a complex task. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel recommendation system integrated into the "WeCare" platform. Leveraging machine learning techniques, including K-Means clustering and the Random Forest algorithm, this system generates personalized diet plans based on an individual’s unique physical attributes, health goals, and special dietary needs, such as those of athletes, bodybuilders, and pregnant women. By considering factors such as body mass index (BMI), calorie requirements, and health objectives, this system empowers individuals to make informed dietary decisions that align with their long-term well-being. This paper outlines the development and implementation of this comprehensive recommendation system, highlighting its potential to enhance lives through data-driven dietary guidance.

articleTitle: A Review on CNN-based Approaches for Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is an illness that has the potential to cause vision impairment in people who are diabetic by affecting the retina's blood vessels. The identification of DR using color fundus images typically relies on the expertise of trained medical professionals to manually detect lesions resulting in time-consuming processes. Along with the growing number of individuals affected by diabetes, there has been an escalating need for dependable diabetic retinopathy screening systems. In the field of artificial intelligence, there have been recent advancements in a specific type of advanced computational model called convolutional neural networks. These networks are designed to mimic the way our brains process visual information, making them effective at tasks involving image data. Their potential extends to various applications including the detection of DR. This paper presents a systematic review of DR detection approaches. The approaches are compared based on the dataset used, accuracy, and methodologies.

articleTitle: Quantitative Nuclei Analysis for Accurate Detection of Breast Abnormalities through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This research explores the essential domain of breast cancer detection by leveraging the capabilities of machine learning algorithms. Breast cancer, a critical global concern, necessitates early identification for effective patient outcomes. This study merges machine learning and medical research for more precise breast cancer detection. Our approach employs machine learning algorithms to differentiate malignant and benign breast cancer cells using quantifiable nuclei attributes from fine needle aspiration images. The dataset contains 569 samples, each with 32 features. Algorithms include AdaBoost, XGBoost and K-Nearest Neighbors with comprehensive data preprocessing including scaling and handling missing values. Techniques like PCA and SMOTE handle class imbalance and high dimensionality. Across scenarios, XGBoost consistently outperforms AdaBoost and KNN in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This research underscores the potential of machine learning in enhancing breast cancer diagnosis, contributing to advanced methodologies that emphasize the significance of quantitative nuclei attributes in accurate detection.

articleTitle: Brewing Better Diagnostics: The Evolution of Tea Disease Identification via Federated CNNs
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are used to identify five kinds of tea leaf illnesses across datasets from five other clients in this research, delving into the world of federated learning. Tea leaf infections remain a problem, especially in areas where tea planting is the mainstay of rural economies while new answers to global issues approach. Using a decentralized methodology, we trained on local datasets (L-1 to L-5) and fed averaged results into a global knowledge base. The customers' performance indicators showed encouraging numbers. For instance, L-1 demonstrated an accuracy of 0.95 and an average precision of 86.71%, recall of 86.47%, and F1-score of 86.55% from a sample size of 507.40. The data from L-4, in contrast, stood out as a model with precision, recall, and F1 scores of 92.34%, 92.06%, and 92.19% across a large sample size of 915.20, supported by an accuracy rate of 0.97. The complex interaction of the Macro, Micro, and Weighted Averages allowed for a comprehensive assessment of individual student and general performance. L-1 to L-5 macro averages were 86.58%, 83.25%, 88.14%, 92.20%, and 90.34%, respectively. For the clients in order, weighted averages with accurate instance representation showed values of 87.98%, 83.39%, 88.25%, 92.24%, and 90.62%. The microforms nearly matched the weighted data, with L-4 retaining its dominance at 92.24%. However, this research's crowning achievement is using federated averaging to transform local insights into a coherent worldwide model. This method highlighted the broader ramifications of using decentralized data while maintaining its essential qualities, advancing the idea that even dispersed common knowledge may come together to build a comprehensive understanding. As a result of the union of federated learning and CNN in the context of diagnosing tea leaf disease, a decentralized but unified strategy for resolving urgent global agricultural concerns has been created.

articleTitle: A Novel Network Intrusion Detection Model using Residual Recurrent Neural Network with Improved Garter Snake-based Optimization Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The data security is considered to be one of the severe difficulties in the emerging internet globe. The data created via the internet is exposed to multiple kinds of exploits and threats. The security approaches like "Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS)" are developed to identify the multiple kinds of attacks and vulnerabilities. Numerous "machine and deep learning" techniques are employed for generating the IDS. The rapid enhancement of computer connectivity and the important amount of computer-based developments enhance in the modern days so the difficulty of satisfying the cyber-city is rising continuously. It also demands an eminent protection mechanism for various cyber threats. Hence, identifying the attacks and the inconsistency in the computer network and enhancing the IDS that work is a powerful part of the cyber security. In this task, a new network "intrusion detection" model is developed to effectively identify the malicious activity of unauthorized users to protect the individual’s computer systems. It helps to reduce the network traffic. The data is accumulated from the internet. The data is subjected to the optimal feature selection phase. Here, the suggested "Enhanced Garter Snake Optimization (EGSO)" algorithm is employed to select the best features. Further, the selected features are forwarded to the detection stage. The intrusion detection is carried out utilizing a Residual Recurrent Neural Network (RRNN) network. The implemented network "intrusion detection" model functionality is contrasted with numerous heuristic algorithms and methods.

articleTitle: Tuberculosis Classification Using EfficientNet B3 Deep Learning Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Tuberculosis is a communicable illness that is transmitted through the inhalation of airborne pathogens between individuals. The main purpose of this study is to categorize Tuberculosis disease using X-ray images. Utilizing the EfficientNetB3 transfer learning model enables the attainment of this objective. The potential of EfficientNetB3 in automatically diagnosing tuberculosis (TB) inside medical images has been highlighted by a recent study. This study introduces a novel methodology that employs EfficientNetB3 to classify photos of tuberculosis (TB) disease into two distinct categories. The methods adopted in this study utilize a dataset including 4,200 photographs. The input photos are used for training the model throughout 40 epochs, utilizing a batch size of 30 and a learning rate of 0.001. The findings derived from our study reveal substantial findings, wherein the proposed EfficientNetB3 model showcases an impressive accuracy rate of 99%. The findings presented in this study show the potential efficacy of EfficientNetB3 as a reliable instrument for the automatic categorization of tuberculosis in X-ray pictures. The implications of the research findings are significant, as achieving high levels of accuracy can significantly enhance the rapid and accurate identification of tuberculosis (TB), leading to enhanced patient outcomes and more successful strategies for disease management. Moreover, the successful implementation of this model underscores the importance of employing advanced deep learning techniques in examining medical images, hence opening up new possibilities for developing intelligent diagnostic tools in the healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Efficient Brain Tumor Segmentation in MRI Images: A ResNet-based Approach with SegNet Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) stands as one of the extensively tested medical imaging methods utilized for disease detection and diagnosis. It plays a pivotal role in identifying various abnormalities within the human body, including tumors, lesions, and other internal issues. Here, the manual distribution technique consumes more time and the method is complex. Because of this, programmed division strategies are utilized. A precise, productive, and high-level computational division technique is expected for deadly infections like brain tumors from brain X-ray pictures. Therefore, this research work focuses on the effective segmentation of brain tumors from brain tumor MRI datasets via image pre-processing, feature segmentation as well and feature extraction. The data pre-processing undergoes two vital steps namely gray scale conversion and image blurring. The preprocessed images are extracted using ResNet which minimizes diverse decomposition as well as gradient problems. A SegNet model is employed in segmenting the images which paves the way for effective classification. To evaluate the segmentation performances, the ResNet is compared with various other approaches for diverse metrics. The evaluation results demonstrated that the proposed approach attained enhanced segmentation results when compared with other techniques.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Detection and Mitigation of XML SQL Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: XML and SQL injection attacks are occurring very frequently nowadays as developers lack major security measures and awareness for the purpose of securing web applications and documents. Many factors are responsible for these types of attacks and vulnerabilities are the main reasons behind all these types of attacks like urbanisation, environmental degradation and some of the market conditions are responsible for these types of vulnerabilities in the market and lead to such attacks. These may also allow the attackers to gain advantage to overlook the front end of the application by taking advantage of all the vulnerabilities of input fields like usernames, passwords, and important credentials. This research paper covers the detailed study of the occurrence of XML injection attacks on front end development applications, also the detection and mitigation policies employed in the literature. The machine learning based model is presented in this case study for detecting XML SQL injection attacks and the mitigation policies are also discussed. The classification machine learning employed in the research paper are also compared using metrics based on accuracy, precision, Specificity and F-1 Score.

articleTitle: ViT-CD: A Vision Transformer Approach to Vehicle Collision Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Traditional methods for accident detection often struggle to handle the complexities of dynamic scenes and varying lighting conditions, leading to sub-optimal performance in accident detection. Subsequently, Vision Transformers’ self-attention mechanisms can be utilized to capture spatial relationships and contextual information within video frames, introducing an innovative solution for real-time vehicle collision detection in CCTV footage. The model proposed in this paper aims to utilize attention mechanisms within transformers to analyze and interpret visual data, presenting an efficient method for identifying potential collisions. The findings demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed approach in relatively improving accident detection accuracy conclude with high-level insights into future research directions highlight the potential impact of ViT-based systems on enhancing road safety and underscore the need for their continued exploration and development.

articleTitle: Enhancing Personalized Performance through a Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Recommender systems have become vital in managing information overload and boosting user engagement. However, traditional methods rely on fixed user preferences inferred from past interactions, often overlooking the dynamic nature of user behavior. This study introduces a fresh perspective by framing the recommendation process as a slate Markov Decision Process (slate-MDP) and leveraging deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to adapt recommendations through ongoing interactions. The ultimate goal is to enhance user engagement over extended periods in the face of evolving environments. The research involved simulating various preference scenarios and evaluating the performance of two DRL-based algorithms: FullSlateQ, an undecomposed full slate Q-learning approach, and SlateQ, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) with slate decomposition approach. The findings highlight SlateQ’s impressive 10.57% superiority in non-static environments compared to FullSlateQ. Furthermore, both algorithms tend to adopt a short-term approach when employing a moderate discount factor, struggling to optimize long-term user engagement. The application of deep reinforcement learning in dynamic settings showcases substantial advancements in user engagement, emphasizing the real-world relevance of our discoveries.

articleTitle: Enhancing ATM Security and Convenience with Fingerprint-Based Biometric Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: A research study based on biometric authentication is summarized in this research report. The money withdrawal system that uses biometric authentication is the focus of this research. Since fingerprints are readily available, trustworthy, and highly accurate, they are the biometric property that has been picked out of all others. To increase the security and usability of the system, finger print recognition technology is employed for both identification and verification. This research offers a succinct examination of the intellectual underpinnings and organizational design of fingerprint recognition. The fundamental fingerprint recognition system is made up of four stages: enrollment, recognition, capturing the biometric data, and storage. Second, there is an improvement approach used in the pre-processing stage that removes extraneous information and clarifies the ridge structure. Finally, fingerprint features are extracted in the feature extraction stage, which takes as input the results of the pre-processing phase. In the matching phase, the obtained feature is compared to the database template. Lastly, the database has the characteristics of the stags that match.

articleTitle: Depression Detection Using Blood Cortisol Levels with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Depression is a pervasive mental health disorder, and timely and accurate diagnosis is critical for effective treatment. This research explores the feasibility of using blood cortisol levels as a biomarker for detecting depression. Through the utilization of machine learning algorithms, our objective is to construct a predictive model capable of categorizing individuals as either depressed or non-depressed based on their blood cortisol levels. A diverse and well-defined group of participants underwent standardized depression assessments, accompanied by the analysis of their blood samples to determine cortisol levels. Machine learning techniques, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Logistic Regression, among others, were employed to develop and validate the depression detection model. In this fictitious scenario, the test set performance metrics reveal that the SVM model achieved an accuracy of 0.85, precision of 0.82, recall of 0.87, and F1-score of 0.84. The GMM model showed slightly lower metrics, with an F1-score of 0.73, accuracy of 0.68, precision of 0.79, and recall of 0.79. Notably, the CNN model outperformed the others, boasting a remarkable 0.92 F1-score, 0.92 accuracy, 0.91 precision, and 0.93 recall. These results underscore the potential of using machine learning and blood cortisol levels as a reliable and objective tool for early depression detection, thereby enhancing the overall quality of mental health care outcomes.

articleTitle: TrashIntelAI- Garbage Collection Automation using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Garbage collection in urban areas has become a major challenge due to the increase in trash production. New technologies, including the application of deep learning and image processing methods, have been created to solve this problem. In this study, we present an automated garbage collection system that recognizes and categorizes rubbish in real-time using computer vision and machine learning methods. A deep learning model classifies the garbage into several categories, and the system also contains an image processing pipeline that pre-processes incoming photos and extracts relevant data. We executed experiments on a real-world dataset to assess the performance of the suggested solution. The outcomes demonstrate that the suggested approach classifies garbage with a high degree of accuracy. The system can recognize and categorize various waste categories, including recyclables, organic garbage, and non-recyclables, which can then be collected individually for proper disposal. This is made possible by the application of deep learning and image processing algorithms. The suggested approach can potentially increase trash disposal efficiency, reduce waste sent to landfills, and promote a cleaner and healthier environment in metropolitan settings. The burden of garbage collection staff can be reduced, and the danger of harm can be reduced, with real-time monitoring and automated waste collection.

articleTitle: Proposing Investments Based on Fundamental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Recent years have witnessed a surge in interest in utilizing machine learning techniques for stock prediction, with studies showcasing their effectiveness in analyzing historical stock data. This thesis focuses on the Nifty 50 stocks and utilizes 22 years’ worth of quarterly financial data for analysis. Six machine learning algorithms were explored, including XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, CatBoost, MultiVariate Linear Regression, and AdaBoost, with an approach that combines fundamental and technical analysis, prioritizing fundamental analysis. Rather than adopting a global training approach, the researchers opted for local training, developing individual models for each Nifty 50 stock to identify the best-performing model for each specific stock. The analysis demonstrated that machine learning algorithms can establish meaningful connections between past financial data and projected revenues, thus providing valuable economic insights and the potential for stock market predictions based on a fusion of fundamental and technical analysis. Moreover, the thesis extended its research to include the development of a rule-based machine learning model to evaluate the financial health of Nifty 500 companies. The model employed predefined rules and criteria based on established financial principles and industry standards, utilizing various financial indicators such as revenue growth, profitability ratios, liquidity ratios, and debt levels. The model’s output was a health score, enabling objective comparisons and rankings of companies within the Nifty 500 index, empowering investors, analysts, and stakeholders in making informed investment decisions. Further details regarding the specific financial indicators and rules applied in calculating the health scores for Nifty 500 stocks can be found in the thesis.

articleTitle: Ethereum NFT Analysis: Ownership Trends, Collections, and Project Dynamic
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant surge in the popularity of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs), and Ethereum has emerged as one of the prominent platforms for the production and trading of these tokens. The primary objective of this research paper is to conduct a thorough analysis of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) based on the Ethereum blockchain. This analysis will be accomplished by utilizing diverse datasets sourced from Kaggle. This paper aims to examine the trends, market dynamics, and factors that exert influence on the ecosystem of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) specifically within the Ethereum blockchain. This paper employs data analysis and visualization techniques to provide valuable insights into the expansion and potential obstacles encountered by the Ethereum non-fungible token (NFT) market. Moreover, it elucidates the influence of this market on the broader cryptocurrency and art sectors.

articleTitle: Predicting and Analysing Lumpy Skin Disease Using Ensemble of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The economic impact of the infectious bovine virus known as Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) is substantial. Because of the poxvirus that causes LSD, cattle suffer from decreased meat and milk output, higher veterinary bills, and trade restrictions on cattle-related products. The biggest difficulty in managing LSD epidemics is identifying them at an early stage. Because they are laborious and time-consuming, traditional procedures result in delayed responses. Our research paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of ensemble machine learning models for LSD prediction to help overcome these obstacles. Machine learning models have been shown to be valuable in the field of epidemiology due to their ability to successfully analyse complex data. In this research, a number of ensemble models that have been pre-trained on parameters including location, climate, and disease outbreak history. We also use data preparation methods to equalize data and standardize inputs, for a more reliable study. In order to better understand the patterns of LSD spread, data visualization tools like heatmaps and box plots are used. Our studies' overarching goal is to improve disease management measures by making use of ensemble machine learning models and data analysis strategies, which will have positive effects on cattle health and the economic security of the livestock industry.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Quad-Wheeled Robot for Targeted Plant Disease Surveillance in Greenhouses
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Technology is rapidly changing modern agriculture, resembling the Green Revolution of the early 20th century, which ushered in advanced agricultural technologies and practices, resulting in substantial increases in crop yields. The practical 4X4 greenhouse bot, attesting to the cohesive integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), Machine Learning algorithm and Robotics, is at the pinnacle of this change. These smart bots, equipped with various environmental sensors, continuously monitor, and provide real-time alerts, ensuring consistent plant health. Simultaneously, the introduction of powerful computer vision techniques, particularly models like YOLOv8, has heralded a new era of accuracy in agricultural practices. This study offers a quad-wheeled AI-powered robot with a Jetson Xavier NX powered camera module for targeted disease surveillance in greenhouses. It constantly monitors environmental conditions via IoT-equipped sensors, for early disease detection in poly-house farming hold the potential to boost farming efficiency and yields.

articleTitle: Automated Quality Assessment of Mangosteen Fruits Using Multimodal Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In this groundbreaking take a look at, we recommend an revolutionary method for Mangosteen fruit exceptional evaluation the use of a hybrid CNN-RNN model. Our method leverages multimodal deep mastering techniques, integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks with Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-LSTM) to efficiently analyze high-decision Mangosteen fruit pix. The dataset incorporates over one thousand various photos sourced from Kaggle, cautiously segmented into Training, Validation, and Testing Sets, ensuring sturdy model learning. Through high-quality-tuning hyperparameters with the Validation Set, we optimized version overall performance with out overfitting risks. The impartial assessment on the Testing Set demonstrates our model's splendid capability to generate exact and degree-specific captions for Mangosteen fruit snap shots, appropriately figuring out unique levels. Rigorous evaluation of the model's schooling performance the use of container loss, elegance loss, and object loss components suggests dependable item localization and relevant caption technology. The imply Average Precision (mAP) graph exhibits growing accuracy, indicating non-stop model improvement at some stage in training. Our integrated CNN-RNN version gives informative captions for Mangosteen fruit photos, marking a widespread development in automating fruit quality assessment. By bridging modern AI technologies with actual-world agricultural packages, our studies guarantees a extra sustainable and green destiny for agricultural practices. The accurate identification of various stages of Mangosteen end result allows knowledgeable choice-making, main to stepped forward manufacturing and the shipping of top class-great produce to fulfill consumer demands.

articleTitle: Enhancing Prime+Probe Attack Detection Using AI and Machine Learning Techniques for Improved Security
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This research paper explores the complex area of PRIME+PROBE attacks, an advanced kind of cache-based side-channel attack that presents serious security risks. The study includes a thorough analysis of PRIME+PROBE attacks, including a thorough description of their key methods. It also compares various hardware performance counter measurement techniques, providing information on how well they can catch these evasive attacks. An experimental setup for replicating PRIME+PROBE attacks on Intel CPUs is described in order to experimentally evaluate the findings. This configuration offers the framework for obtaining important information and insights. The paper then uses three machine learning techniques to identify PRIME+PROBE attacks utilizing hardware performance counter features: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Network, and Gradient Boosting. The findings of this study provide important light on the capabilities and constraints of machine learning algorithms for countering PRIME+PROBE attacks as well as hardware performance counter measurement instruments. The research makes a substantial contribution to the field of cybersecurity and lays the groundwork for the creation of effective defenses against these elusive and possibly catastrophic threats.

articleTitle: Modernizing Data Processing: CNNs and OCR for Automated Document Classification and Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The growing use of identification documents such as Aadhar cards in the digital age has underlined the significance of creating simplified methods for automated classification and data extraction. In this paper, we present a comprehensive exploration and practical implementation of cutting-edge technologies aimed at revolutionizing data analysis, information retrieval, and automation, particularly in the context of identifying documents such as Aadhar cards in the digital age. Our approach integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for classification and the Tesseract OCR engine for data extraction, demonstrating their combined potential for driving significant advancements. We systematically tested and optimized various architectural elements, including different layer configurations, dropout rates, batch normalization placements, and regularizers. Through meticulous experimentation, we achieved remarkable results and substantial progress across multiple dimensions. Notably, our final model, strategically leveraging a hybrid optimization strategy involving SGD, RMSprop, and Adam optimizers, along with architectural refinements, attained an impressive accuracy of 97.52%. This accomplishment underscores the effectiveness of our approach in automated classification and data extraction tasks.

articleTitle: Sequential Transfer Learning Model for Pneumonia Detection Using Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This work utilises a sequential convolutional neural network (CNN) model for the detection of Pneumonia in chest X-ray images, focusing on improving diagnostic accuracy. The model utilises transfer learning, utilising a pre-trained neural network architecture to achieve the highest accuracy rate of 92.15% on the test dataset. Moreover, this represents a significant advancement over prior methodologies, which attained an accuracy of 90.22%. The robust precision, recall, and F1-score metrics highlighted the model’s performance, affirming its proficiency in distinguishing between pneumonia (a medical condition) and normal (a healthy state) cases. This research contributes to medical diagnostics, offering a promising solution for healthcare professionals in their quest for improved pneumonia detection from chest X-ray images. Moreover, the work identifies potential areas for further refinement, encompassing hyperparameter optimisation, improved interpretability techniques, and practical deployment, all aimed at elevating the utility of this transfer learning model in medical diagnostics and overall healthcare. This research signifies a notable significant advancement in utilising the power of deep learning for medical disease detection.

articleTitle: Real-Time License Plate Detection and Recognition System using YOLOv7x and EasyOCR
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Automated license plate detection system is used for recognition and locating of license plates on vehicles using image processing and computer vision methods. Automated license plate detection is an important area of research in computer vision with far-reaching applications in the industrial sector. It has the potential to increase productivity and accuracy in numerous industrial applications. The procedure entails utilizing a camera to take a photo of a vehicle's license plate, processing the photo to identify the plate, and extracting the characters from the plate. This paper provides implementation of the YOLOv7x algorithm to detect license plate on vehicles. EasyOCR is applied to the detected license plate to recognize the text. The model is trained on a customized dataset consisting of only Indian vehicles license plate. The proposed work achieves a high accuracy of 99% and outperforms old techniques like Yolov3, darknet, CNN.

articleTitle: Research on Manipulator Control Strategy based on PPO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: With the continuous development of science and technology, as a common industrial robot automation equipment, the research on its control strategy has always been a hot spot in related fields, but there is a problem of inaccurate result evaluation. Traditional control algorithms cannot solve the problem of adaptive training learning in complex high-dimensional environments, and the evaluation is unreasonable. Therefore, this paper proposes a PPO algorithm for innovative optimization control system analysis. First, the manipulator control theory is used to evaluate the manipulator and carry out it according to the requirements of the control system Indicator division to reduce interference factors in the control system. Then, the manipulator control related theory analyzes the manipulator control system, forms the control system scheme, and corrects Comprehensive analysis of control system results. The simulation environment reference shows that under the condition of certain evaluation criteria, the PPO algorithm has an accuracy on the control system of the robotic arm The real-time performance of the control algorithm is better than that of the traditional control algorithm.

articleTitle: Child Abuse Detection Using a Low-Cost Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: "Too much information is no information." Security cameras are common these days. However, an excessive number of cameras can overwhelm a human operator’s attention and reduce the chance to observe any behavior related to child abuse. By adding a low-cost Nvidia Jetson Nano 4G developer kit to an existing CCTV, the system described here can detect and highlight possible child abuse behavior in a summarized list. The list can reduce the human operator workload and increase the chance of pinpointing a child abuse case. This child abuse detection system is currently being used in childcare centers.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Breast Tumour Diagnosis & Classification from Fine-Tuned EfficientNetB3 Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: This study uses cutting-edge digital image processing techniques to diagnose and categorize breast tumours. By using the EfficientNetB3 transfer learning model and including fine-tuning layers, this research aims to improve the precision and effectiveness of breast tumour diagnosis. The dataset utilized in this research consists of 1134 breast ultrasound pictures, classified into three categories: normal breast tissue, benign tumours, and malignant tumours. The dataset has been carefully partitioned into training, validation, and test subgroups to assist the model's creation and assessment. The pre-existing EfficientNetB3 model is adapted and optimized through transfer learning to specifically cater to analyzing breast ultrasound pictures. The use of fine-tuning layers allows for the adaptation of the model to the distinctive attributes associated with breast tumour diagnosis. Throughout the training phase, the examination of accuracy and loss graphs offers valuable insights into the learning process of the model. This analysis facilitates the prompt determination of any possible difficulties that may arise. The research culminates with assessing the predictive model's efficacy on the test subgroup. A constructed confusion matrix provides a complete evaluative instrument, facilitating the computation of measures such as accuracy. The subsequent stage demonstrates the model's capabilities, giving insight into its possible implications for treatment. The initial results suggest that the proposed technique has shown an accuracy of 88%, highlighting its potential. Although this study shows potential, it also highlights the need for more research in several areas, such as dataset expansion, exploration of other architectures, and incorporation of clinical perspectives. Integrating advanced technology and medical diagnostics presents novel opportunities for enhancing breast tumour diagnosis. The fine-tuned EfficientNetB3 transfer learning model has shown promise as a vital asset in the battle against breast tumours.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Islanding Identification Scheme for a Grid Integrated PV System
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Integrating DG systems with the grid introduces substantial challenges, such as power quality issues and the risk of involuntary islanding events. Timely detection and isolation of DG systems from the utility grid during islanding scenarios are critical. Islanding events can expose grid personnel to electric shock hazards and potentially damage equipment during out-of-phase re-closure. In the context of distributed generators, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are employed to detect islanding events. LSTMs, a type of recurrent neural network, capture and analyze time-series data from generators to identify abnormal operational conditions, such as islanding, where a generator operates independently from the main grid. By learning patterns and dependencies in the data, LSTMs can effectively distinguish between normal and islanded states, providing a robust and reliable method for real-time islanding detection, enhancing grid stability and safety. The performance is assessed through simulation experiments conducted using MATLAB 2023a software, demonstrating its superior effectiveness compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Indian Driving Scene Description Generator Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Driving scene description generation plays a crucial role in various applications, including driver assistance systems, traffic monitoring and autonomous driving. This study proposes a comprehensive approach for driving scene description generation using deep learning (DL) techniques. The methodology involves the collection and preprocessing of a large-scale driving scene dataset, which consists of diverse driving scenarios captured from dashcam videos. The dataset is carefully labelled for different scene categories, such as highways, urban areas, night scenes, and rural roads. Frames from video datasets are collected and are captioned for DL-Model for various scene. In addition, DL-based approaches are employed to leverage the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for scene detection. The CNN architecture, such as VGGNet-16 is evaluated to extract high-level features and enable accurate scene captioning from recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures such as LSTM and GRU for caption generation. The evaluation of the proposed DL models is done using BLEU score. The scores depict the level of effectiveness of the approach in accurate generation of captions for driving scenes, achieving high performance across various scene categories. The system can be deployed on embedded platforms or integrated into existing driver assistance systems to enhance situational awareness and improve decision-making processes.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing, Big Data, and Secure Data Sharing enabled through Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The security issues of data and information have grown extremely significant in the context of the accelerated growth of information technology. In everyday web browsing or interactions, information and data may be compromised. When sharing data, it is important to examine the security features of the secure data-sharing system. The purpose of this paper is to investigate the security mechanisms of cloud computing-oriented big data sharing systems in the Internet of Things age. This paper introduced the attribute-driven encryption (ADE) technique, provided an in-depth description of the ADE technique, and examined security issues in cloud computing big data sharing. According to the testing data, the ADE technique consumes a mean of 11 seconds with five attempts, while the additional 2 approaches use 51.8 & 31.6 seconds, respectively ADEs use lesser duration and are far more effective than the additional 2 techniques for various encryption values beneath identical data. As a result, ADE techniques must possess a competitive edge.

articleTitle: Research on Humanoid Robot Recognition and Imitation of Human Action based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: The role of recognition and imitation of human actions in humanoid robots is very important, but there is a problem of inaccurate recognition and imitation. Ordinary methods cannot solve the problem of recognizing and imitating human movements in humanoid robots, and the methods are unreasonable. Therefore, this paper proposes a machine learning to recognize and imitate human motion analysis. First of all, artificial intelligence is used to inspect the robot, and the indicators are divided according to the requirements of recognizing and imitating human actions to reduce them Identify and imitate interference factors in human movements. Then, artificial intelligence detects the humanoid robot to recognize and imitate human actions, forms a recognition and imitation of human action schemes, and recognizes and imitates human action results Conduct a comprehensive analysis. MATLAB simulation shows that under certain evaluation criteria, machine learning can recognize and imitate the accuracy of human movements of humanoid robots The time to recognize and imitate human movements is better than ordinary methods.

articleTitle: Efficient Vehicle Detection and Classification using YOLO v8 for Real-Time Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: In the realm of real-time applications such as autonomous driving and surveillance, efficient vehicle detection stands as a paramount concern. The revolutionary You Only Look Once (YOLO) framework, renowned for its rapid object recognition, has reshaped this landscape. This study delves into the fusion of real-time vehicle detection and YOLO v8, optimizing its architecture for swift and precise identification. Empirical validation underscores the model's prowess, achieving a remarkable accuracy of 97.9% on mAP50 and 91.3% on mAP50-95. This achievement not only attests to the model's accuracy but also reaffirms its real-time processing capabilities. The implications resonate across transportation safety and urban planning, promising transformative potential. This research underscores the power of YOLO v8 in intelligent object detection, poised to reshape and enhance various domains.

articleTitle: A Review on Software Defined Networks: Energy Efficient Load Balancing Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Elements of the Internet's traditional architecture are currently immovable, a phenomenon known as "ossification of the Internet," which has created significant challenges for the implementation of IPv6 and made employing IP multicast services challenging. The Internet still needs to be expanded for a variety of reasons, including enhancing network's higher availability, offering users transport layer connectivity, and network resources quality of service can be managed dynamically for naive applications like data centres, cloud computing, and network virtualization. The Future Internet's next-generation design has proposed the idea of Software Defined Networking (SDN) to meet these needs. This decoupling enables the deployment of control plane software components, such as the Open Flow controller, on computer platforms that are significantly more powerful than conventional network hardware, such as switches and routers, while safeguarding the information. To address the many obstacles to creating the advanced Internet and to tackle the issue of the Current Internet, an understanding of SDN Paradigm is necessary. This article covers current technologies and the vast range of cutting-edge initiatives on SDN to fulfil these criteria. This is followed by an in-depth examination of the key difficulties in this field. SDN is an architectural strategy for networking that attempts to make networks more responsive, adaptable, and programmable. Instead of depending on manual configuration of individual networking devices, this separation enables network administrators and operators to manage and configure network resources in a centralized manner using software. The control and data planes of network devices like routers and switches are integrated in a typical networking architecture. While the data plane is in charge of handling the actual forwarding of packets, the control plane is in charge of determining routing decisions and overseeing the network's overall behaviour.

articleTitle: Quality of Service Based Performance Evaluation of Controllers in Software Defined Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Controllers are deployed on the control layer of the Software Defined Architecture. Each controller has vital functionalities according to the topologies and traffic of the network. The controller displays different types of performance while used under different topologies. The controllers are fed with a snippet of the code which is under a planned process and the controller start serving according to the code snippet. In this paper a comparison of open source controllers POX, NOX, BEACON, RYU, Floodlight and Opendaylight is simulated in Mininet SDN emulator. The QoS parameters are Round Trip Time (RTT), Average Delay, Jitter, Bitrate, Throughput, Loss of Packets and Latency. The results show that Opendaylight with 95% confidence level tops the list of the controllers in heavy traffic network, rest no significant change in performance is recorded..

articleTitle: Learning Rate Regularized EfficientNet based Rice Grain Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: One of the most popular grain items cultivated across the globe is rice. Rice seeds may be recognized by their appearance, form, and ethnicity. Rice types may be distinguished owing to their various traits. This rice category assessment relates to the seed efficiency, which includes various hereditary pairings. Along with population development, there is a rise in the demand for rice, thus farmers require high-quality rice grains. Due to the variety of rice grain instances currently available on the market, rice grain classification becomes crucial. A significant amount of time and effort might be consumed on manual classification of grains. The technological innovations could be utilized to automatically identify rice grain images and provide grain categorization based on grain features. This paper suggests Learning Rate Regularized Efficient Net (LRR-EN) to classify the rice grain more efficiently. The 30,000 Rice images of Rice Image Dataset from Kaggle is used in the suggested model. The examination of image distribution is the first step in the LRR-EN model. The best CNN model is selected by fitting the rice images with existing CNN models after image augmentation. When compared to other CNN models, the Efficient Net demonstrated an accuracy of 92.41%. The learning rate parameter was now fine-tuned to increase accuracy using the EfficientNet CNN. The augmented rice images are fitted to LRR-EN using several learning rates, such as 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1. The experimental findings reveal that, when compared to different learning rates, the suggested LRR-EN with a 0.001 learning rate demonstrates the greatest Accuracy of 99.01%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Distributed Generation and Virtual STATCOM System Organization and Control A Comprehensive Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Conference on Information Technologies and Communications (GCITC)
abstract: Voltage stability in the distribution system is jeopardized by the growing number of DG connections. Stabilize voltage via reactive power compensators like STATCOM. The intricate design of STATCOM's distribution system makes installation a challenging task. If not properly positioned, the system's economic efficiency and availability might be negatively affected. This work proposes a method for Virtual STATCOM Configuration and Control that enables several DGs to function as a single STATCOM. Virtual STATCOM makes advantage of preexisting power facilities rather than constructing new ones. This eliminates the complexity in the distribution system, which is a major obstacle to installation, and makes it cost-effective. In contrast to traditional STATCOM, which only manages the power quality-of the access-point, E-STATCOM regulates a large number of DGs connected to the system in order to modify the PCC's power quality. A linear programming configuration is used to set up the Virtual STATCOM integrated control mechanism.
